Special Category: For Grab, Uber, etc.
Covers: - Enhanced liability (transporting passengers for hire) - Increased risks of passenger transport - Higher usage/mileage
Required: Cannot use personal car insurance for commercial e-hailing.




Definition: Discount for not making claims.
Accumulation: - Year 1 no claim: 25% NCD - Year 2 no claim: 30% NCD - Year 3 no claim: 38.33% NCD - Year 4 no claim: 45% NCD - Year 5+ no claim: 55% NCD (maximum)
Transfer: Can transfer NCD to new vehicle if same owner.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 10 (Links to Section 7.3.5 - NCD)
Question: “To capitalize on no claim discount for motor cover, the following must be performed: A. Increase in premium as mandated must be paid B. No claim discount applies beyond basic premium C. Evidence of entitlement from previous insurer must be obtained ✅ D. All the above”
Answer: C (Evidence of entitlement required)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Must PROVE NCD entitlement from previous insurer!
ANALYSIS:
C ✅ CORRECT: - Must obtain NCD certificate from previous insurer - Proves claim-free record - Required for NCD transfer - Cannot just claim verbally
Example:
Switching insurers:
Old Insurer: 3 years no claim (38.33% NCD)
New Insurer: Requires NCD certificate from old insurer
Without certificate: Start from 0% NCD
With certificate: Continue with 38.33% NCD
A ❌ Wrong: - NCD = DISCOUNT (reduces premium) - Not an increase in premium - Opposite concept
B ❌ Misleading: - NCD applies TO the premium (reduces it) - Not “beyond” basic premium - Unclear statement
KEYWORDS: - “Evidence of entitlement” = NCD certificate - “Previous insurer” = Transfer proof - “Must be obtained” = Required documentation
MEMORY TIP: “No Proof, No Discount” (need certificate)




Key Change: From tariffed rates to risk-based pricing.
Details: - Insurers can set own premiums based on risk assessment - Factors: Driving record, vehicle type, usage, location - Promotes competition - Encourages safe driving - Minimum premium: RM20 (still applicable for tariff products)




What’s NOT Covered: - Wear and tear - Mechanical/electrical breakdown - Driving under influence of alcohol/drugs - Unauthorized drivers - Use for illegal purposes - Negligent maintenance - Consequential losses







Five Main Types:

Fire and Special Perils
All Risk Insurance
Business Interruption/Consequential Loss
Houseowners Insurance
Burglary Insurance




Covers: - Fire damage - Lightning - Explosion/implosion - Aircraft damage - Impact by vehicles - Riot, strike, malicious damage
Excludes: - War, terrorism - Nuclear risks - Wear and tear - Consequential losses (lost profits)
Example:
Factory catches fire:
Building damage: RM500,000 ✅ Covered
Machinery damage: RM200,000 ✅ Covered
Lost profits (3 months): RM300,000 ❌ NOT covered (need Business Interruption)




Purpose: Cover lost profits due to property damage.
Covers: - Lost gross profit - Increased cost of working - Fixed costs continuing during interruption
Trigger: Must be property damage covered by underlying policy (e.g., fire).

📝 EXAM QUESTION 2 (Links to Section 7.4.A.III - Business Interruption)
Question: “Mr. Hew compensated when machine broke down. Amount covers loss of profits due to production interruption. What policy? A. Machinery Breakdown (Loss of Profit) Policy ✅ B. Fire (Consequential Loss) Policy C. Machinery & Equipment Policy D. Liability (Loss of Profit) Policy”
Answer: A (Machinery Breakdown Loss of Profit)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Loss of PROFITS from MACHINERY breakdown = Specific policy!
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ CORRECT: - Machinery Breakdown (Loss of Profit) Policy - Covers lost profits when machinery breaks down - Consequential loss from equipment failure - Exactly what question describes
B ❌ Wrong trigger: - Fire (Consequential Loss) = Lost profits from FIRE - Not machinery breakdown - Different peril
C ❌ Wrong coverage: - Machinery & Equipment = PHYSICAL damage to machine - Does NOT cover lost profits - Only repair/replacement costs
D ❌ No such policy: - Liability insurance covers legal liability to others - Not loss of profits from own machinery
POLICY MATCHING:
PHYSICAL Damage Coverage:
Machinery & Equipment Policy = Repair/replace machine

CONSEQUENTIAL Coverage (Lost Profits):
Machinery Breakdown (Loss of Profit) = Income loss from breakdown

Must have BOTH for complete protection!
KEYWORDS: - “Loss of profits” = Consequential coverage - “Machine broke down” = Machinery breakdown trigger - “Interruption of production” = Business interruption
MEMORY TIP: “Machine breaks → Profit lost → Loss of Profit Policy”




IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:



Aspect
Houseowners
Householders




Insured
Property OWNER
TENANT/Occupier


Building Coverage
✅ YES
❌ NO


Contents Coverage
✅ YES
✅ YES


Liability
✅ Owner’s liability
✅ Occupier’s liability



Example:
Mr. Lee OWNS house: Houseowners policy
- Building structure ✅
- Contents ✅
- Owner's liability ✅

Mr. Tan RENTS apartment: Householders policy
- Building ❌ (landlord's responsibility)
- Contents ✅
- Tenant's liability ✅





Purpose: Protect against legal liability to third parties.
Main Types:

Public Liability - General public/visitors
Product Liability - Defective products
Professional Indemnity - Professional errors
Directors & Officers (D&O) - Management decisions
Employer’s Liability - Employees (workplace accidents)
Workmen’s Compensation - Statutory coverage for workmen




Purpose: Cover employer’s legal liability for employee accidents.
What’s Covered: - Employer’s negligence - Breach of duty (safety measures) - Common law liability
What’s NOT Covered: - Employee’s own negligence (unless employer also negligent) - Statutory liability under Workmen’s Compensation Act

📝 EXAM QUESTION 7 (Links to Section 7.4.D.VI - Employer’s Liability)
Question: “Which falls under Employer’s Liability Policy? Employer’s liability for accidents to employee from: i. Employer’s personal negligence ii. Employer’s breach of duty (safety measures) iii. Employee’s own negligence
A. I only B. II only C. I & II only ✅ D. I & III only”
Answer: C (I & II only)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Employer’s Liability covers EMPLOYER’S fault, not employee’s own negligence!
ANALYSIS:
i. Employer’s personal negligence ✅ COVERED: - Employer failed to supervise properly - Employer gave unsafe instructions - Employer’s direct actions caused accident - EMPLOYER AT FAULT
ii. Employer’s breach of duty (safety) ✅ COVERED: - Failed to provide safe working environment - Inadequate safety equipment - No safety training - Poor maintenance - EMPLOYER FAILED DUTY OF CARE
iii. Employee’s own negligence ❌ NOT COVERED: - Employee was careless - Employee ignored safety rules - Employee’s own fault - NO EMPLOYER LIABILITY (employee responsible)
PRINCIPLE:
Employer's Liability Insurance:
Covers: Employer's FAULT ✅
Does NOT cover: Employee's FAULT ❌

Rationale: Employer only liable when employer at fault
EXAMPLE SCENARIOS:
Scenario 1: ✅ COVERED
Worker falls from height
Reason: Employer didn't provide safety harness
Result: EMPLOYER'S breach of duty (covered)

Scenario 2: ✅ COVERED
Worker injured by faulty machine
Reason: Employer failed to maintain equipment
Result: EMPLOYER'S negligence (covered)

Scenario 3: ❌ NOT COVERED
Worker ignores warning signs, gets injured
Reason: Worker's own negligence
No employer breach of duty
Result: NOT covered (employee at fault)
KEYWORDS: - “Employer’s negligence” = Employer at fault ✅ - “Employer’s breach of duty” = Employer failed obligation ✅ - “Employee’s own negligence” = Employee at fault ❌
MEMORY TIP: “Employer’s Liability = Employer’s FAULT only”




Legal Requirement: Employers MUST cover “workmen” without SOCSO.
Purpose: Statutory compensation for workplace injuries.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 6 (Links to Section 7.4.D.VII - Workmen’s Compensation)
Question: “Which TRUE under Workmen’s Compensation Policy as according to law? A. Employer must cover employees classified as ‘workmen’ and without SOCSO ✅ B. Employer must cover employees with SOCSO C. No legal requirement to cover workmen D. Fixed amount to cover all workmen”
Answer: A (Workmen without SOCSO must be covered)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Workmen’s Compensation is for employees NOT covered by SOCSO!
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ CORRECT: - Employers MUST insure “workmen” - BUT: Only if NOT covered by SOCSO - Two separate systems: - SOCSO = Social security (most employees) - Workmen’s Comp = Insurance (workmen not in SOCSO)
WHO ARE “WORKMEN”?: - Manual laborers - Certain categories of workers - Earning below specified amount - NOT covered by SOCSO
B ❌ Wrong - mutually exclusive: - If employee HAS SOCSO → NO Workmen’s Comp needed - SOCSO provides coverage already - Would be double coverage
C ❌ False - it IS required: - Workmen’s Compensation Act REQUIRES coverage - Legal obligation for employers - Penalties for non-compliance
D ❌ Not fixed amount: - Coverage varies by wages, risk category - Not a fixed amount for all
COVERAGE FRAMEWORK:
Employee Categories:

SOCSO-covered employees:
→ Protected by SOCSO ✅
→ NO Workmen's Comp needed ❌

"Workmen" without SOCSO:
→ NOT protected by SOCSO ❌
→ MUST have Workmen's Comp ✅

Purpose: Ensure ALL employees protected
KEYWORDS: - “Workmen” = Specific employee category - “Without SOCSO” = Gap that needs filling - “Must cover” = Legal requirement
MEMORY TIP: “No SOCSO → Need Workmen’s Comp” (ensure protection)





Three Main Types:

Contractor’s All Risks (CAR)
Erection All Risks (EAR)
Machinery Breakdown




Purpose: Protect construction projects during building phase.
Covers: - Construction works - Materials on site - Equipment used - Third-party liability
Typical Projects: Buildings, bridges, roads, tunnels.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 1 (Links to Section 7.4.E.I - CAR Insurance)
Question: “Mr. Kanesan asks for policy covering faulty design/construction of machines and damage during installation. Which suitable? A. Machinery Breakdown Policy B. Contractor’s All Risks Policy ✅ C. Comprehensive Machine Policy D. Loss of Profit policy”
Answer: B (Contractor’s All Risks)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: During INSTALLATION = Construction phase = CAR policy!
ANALYSIS:
B ✅ CORRECT - CAR Policy: - “During installation” = Construction/erection phase ✅ - “Faulty design/construction” = Construction risks ✅ - Covers work in progress - Includes installation damage
A ❌ Machinery Breakdown: - For OPERATIONAL machines (after installation) - Not during installation/construction - Wrong phase
C ❌ Comprehensive Machine: - For machines IN USE (operational) - Not installation phase - Wrong coverage period
D ❌ Loss of Profit: - Consequential loss (lost income) - Not physical damage during construction - Wrong coverage type
PHASE MATCHING:
CONSTRUCTION PHASE (installing/building):
→ Contractor's All Risks (CAR) ✅
→ Erection All Risks (EAR) ✅

OPERATIONAL PHASE (after installed, in use):
→ Machinery Breakdown ✅
→ Machinery & Equipment ✅

CONSEQUENTIAL (lost profits):
→ Loss of Profit policies ✅
KEYWORDS: - “Damage during installation” = Construction phase - “Faulty design/construction” = CAR coverage - “Machines” = Could be EAR too, but CAR covers broader construction
MEMORY TIP: “Installing = CAR/EAR; Operating = Machinery policies”

📝 EXAM QUESTION 8 (Links to Section 7.4.E - CAR Exclusions)
Question: “Key exclusions of Contractor’s All Risk Policy: i. Loss due to war ii. Loss due to wilful act of insured iii. Loss due to nuclear radiation
A. I only B. I & II only C. I & III only D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: CAR excludes WAR, WILFUL ACTS, and NUCLEAR risks!
ANALYSIS:
i. War ✅ EXCLUDED: - War, invasion, civil war - Uninsurable risk (catastrophic) - Standard exclusion all policies
ii. Wilful act of insured ✅ EXCLUDED: - Intentional damage by insured - Fraud prevention - Moral hazard control - Cannot profit from own wrongdoing
iii. Nuclear radiation ✅ EXCLUDED: - Nuclear incident, radioactive contamination - Catastrophic risk - Uninsurable - Standard exclusion
COMMON EXCLUSIONS IN GENERAL INSURANCE:
Almost ALL general insurance excludes:
❌ War and war-like operations
❌ Nuclear risks
❌ Intentional acts by insured
❌ Wear and tear
❌ Inherent vice

These are STANDARD exclusions
KEYWORDS: - “War” = Catastrophic, uninsurable - “Wilful act” = Intentional damage (moral hazard) - “Nuclear” = Catastrophic risk
MEMORY TIP: “WON’T cover War, Own Acts, Nuclear” (WON acronym)




Purpose: Cover installation/erection of machinery and equipment.
Covers: - Installation of plant and machinery - Testing and commissioning - Damage during erection - Third-party liability
Difference from CAR: EAR = Machinery installation; CAR = Building construction.





Definition: Guarantee that party will fulfill contractual obligations.
Three Main Construction Bonds (MEMORIZE):

Tender Bond
Performance Bond
Advance Payment Bond


📝 EXAM QUESTION 3, 4, 5 (Links to Section 7.4.F - Bonds)
Question 3: “Which NOT a type of bond in construction? A. Tender Bond B. Performance C. Banking Security Bond ✅ D. Advance Payment Bond”
Answer: C (Banking Security Bond - NOT construction bond)
Question 4: “Which bond required for submission of tenders? A. Tender Bond ✅ B. Performance C. Banking Security Bond D. Advance Payment Bond”
Answer: A (Tender Bond)
Question 5: “Which bond ensures contractor fulfills duties within specified period? A. Tender Bond B. Performance ✅ C. Banking Security Bond D. Advance Payment Bond”
Answer: B (Performance Bond)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: THREE construction bonds - Tender, Performance, Advance Payment!

COMPREHENSIVE BOND ANALYSIS:
1. TENDER BOND (Question 4):
Purpose: Guarantee bidder will honor tender if accepted.
When Required: Submission of tender/bid for contract.
Protects: Project owner (principal) against contractor backing out.
Amount: Usually 2-5% of tender value.
Example:
Company submits tender for RM10 million project
Tender Bond: RM200,000 (2%)

If company wins but backs out:
Principal keeps RM200,000 (compensates for wasted time/re-tendering)

2. PERFORMANCE BOND (Question 5):
Purpose: Ensure contractor completes project as specified.
When Required: After contract awarded, during project execution.
Protects: Owner against contractor default, delays, poor quality.
Amount: Usually 10% of contract value.
Example:
Building contract: RM10 million
Performance Bond: RM1 million (10%)

If contractor abandons project or fails to complete:
Owner claims RM1 million to hire another contractor

3. ADVANCE PAYMENT BOND:
Purpose: Guarantee refund if contractor doesn’t perform after receiving advance.
When Required: When contractor receives upfront payment.
Protects: Owner’s advance payment.
Amount: Usually equals advance payment amount.
Example:
Contract: RM10 million
Advance payment: RM2 million (20%)
Advance Payment Bond: RM2 million

If contractor takes money and doesn't work:
Owner claims RM2 million back from bond

4. BANKING SECURITY BOND (Question 3) - ❌ NOT A CONSTRUCTION BOND: - NOT specific to construction industry - General banking/financial guarantee - WRONG ANSWER (this is the trap!)

BOND SEQUENCE IN PROJECT:
PROJECT LIFECYCLE:

STEP 1: Tendering
→ TENDER BOND (ensure serious bidders)

STEP 2: Contract Award
→ PERFORMANCE BOND (ensure completion)
→ ADVANCE PAYMENT BOND (if advance given)

STEP 3: Project Execution
→ Bonds remain active until completion

STEP 4: Completion
→ Bonds released
KEYWORDS: - “Tender” = Bidding stage - “Performance” = Execution/completion - “Advance Payment” = Protect upfront payment - “Banking Security” = NOT construction bond
MEMORY TIP:
TAP for Construction:
T = Tender Bond (bidding)
A = Advance Payment Bond (upfront $)
P = Performance Bond (completion)




Other Types: - Money Insurance (cash in transit) - Fidelity Guarantee (employee dishonesty) - Plate Glass Insurance - Electronic Equipment Insurance - Cyber Insurance (data breach, cyber attacks)





Personal Accident (PA) Insurance
Medical Insurance (covered in Chapter 5)
Travel Insurance






📝 EXAM QUESTION 9 (Links to Section 7.3 - Motor Insurance Rules)
Question: “Rules governing motor insurance Malaysia. Identify correct: i. No official receipt required ii. Post-dated cheques can be accepted iii. Premiums received within 7 days from risk commences
A. I & II only B. I, II & III only C. I & IV only D. All the above”
Answer: C (Wait - seems error in question, “IV” not listed)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Cash Before Cover principle - payment BEFORE coverage starts!
CORRECT RULES:
Cash Before Cover Principle: - Premium must be paid BEFORE coverage starts - Official receipt MUST be issued - Post-dated cheques generally NOT accepted (payment must clear) - No credit extended
LIKELY ANSWER: Based on standard practice, proper rules are: - Official receipt IS required ✅ - Post-dated cheques NOT accepted ❌ - Premium paid BEFORE cover (not after 7 days) ✅
Note: Question may have formatting error. Standard rule = “Cash before cover, no credit”.

title: Chapter 7: General Insurance Products in Insurance Planning
text:
General insurance protects against financial losses from specific risks. Unlike life insurance (person), general insurance covers PROPERTY, LIABILITY, and specific PERILS. This chapter covers motor, property, marine, liability, engineering insurance and more.
Exam Weight: 12-15% of total exam
Study Time Recommendation: 7-9 hours

title: Chapter 7: General Insurance Products in Insurance Planning
text:
By the end of this chapter, you must be able to:

Explain three core general insurance principles (Indemnity, Contribution, Subrogation)
Distinguish motor insurance types (Act, Third Party, Comprehensive)
Identify property insurance types (Fire, All Risk, Business Interruption)
Understand liability insurance categories
Explain engineering insurance (CAR, EAR, Machinery Breakdown)
Know bonds types (Tender, Performance, Advance Payment)
Apply general insurance in financial planning

title: Chapter 7: General Insurance Products in Insurance Planning
text:
CRITICAL FRAMEWORK (HIGH EXAM FREQUENCY):
THREE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES
├── 1. INDEMNITY (Restore to original position)
├── 2. CONTRIBUTION (Share among insurers)
└── 3. SUBROGATION (Recover from third party)



Definition: Restore insured to financial position BEFORE loss - no profit, no loss.
Key Points: - Compensation = ACTUAL LOSS only - Cannot profit from insurance - Prevents unjust enrichment - Based on replacement/repair cost
Example:
House damaged by fire:
Original value: RM200,000
Damage: RM50,000 repairs needed

Insurance pays: RM50,000 (actual loss)
NOT: RM200,000 (full value)
NOT: RM60,000 (more than loss)

Result: House restored to pre-loss condition
What Indemnity Means: - Cannot claim more than loss - Cannot rebuild better than before - Cannot upgrade using insurance money - Return to SAME condition, not improved
📌 EXAM TIP: Indemnity = Compensate ACTUAL loss, no profit for insured.




Definition: When multiple policies cover same risk, insurers share claim proportionally.
Key Points: - Can have multiple policies on same asset - Cannot claim MORE than loss from all policies combined - Each insurer pays proportionate share - Prevents over-compensation
Formula:
Contribution = (Policy A Sum / Total Sum Insured) × Loss

Example:
Fire destroys warehouse worth RM500,000
Policy A: RM300,000
Policy B: RM200,000
Total: RM500,000

Loss: RM100,000

Policy A pays: (RM300,000 / RM500,000) × RM100,000 = RM60,000
Policy B pays: (RM200,000 / RM500,000) × RM100,000 = RM40,000
Total: RM100,000
Example Scenario:
Car insured with:
Insurer A: RM80,000
Insurer B: RM60,000
Total: RM140,000

Accident damage: RM28,000

Insurer A pays: (80/140) × 28,000 = RM16,000
Insurer B pays: (60/140) × 28,000 = RM12,000
Total: RM28,000 (actual loss)
📌 EXAM TIP: Contribution ensures fair sharing among multiple insurers - no double compensation.




Definition: After paying claim, insurer can recover from responsible third party.
Key Points: - Insurer “steps into shoes” of insured - Can sue third party for recovery - Only after insured fully compensated - Prevents insured from double recovery
When Applies: - Third party caused the loss - Third party legally liable - After insurer pays claim - Insured must cooperate
Example:
Your car hit by negligent driver:
Damage: RM20,000

STEP 1: Your insurer pays you RM20,000 (you're made whole)
STEP 2: Your insurer sues negligent driver (subrogation)
STEP 3: Insurer recovers RM20,000 from driver
STEP 4: Insurer keeps recovery (recoups claim payment)

You benefit: Immediate payment without lawsuit
Insurer benefit: Recovers claim cost
Negligent party: Pays for damage caused
Important: - Does NOT apply to life insurance (non-indemnity) - Insured cannot compromise third party’s liability - Insured must assist insurer in recovery
📌 EXAM TIP: Subrogation = Insurer’s right to recover from liable third party AFTER paying claim.





General Insurance Classification:
GENERAL INSURANCE
├── 1. MOTOR INSURANCE
│   └── Vehicles, accidents, liability
└── 2. NON-MOTOR INSURANCE
    ├── Property (Fire, Burglary, All Risk)
    ├── Marine (Hull, Cargo)
    ├── Liability (Public, Professional)
    ├── Engineering (CAR, EAR, Machinery)
    └── Others (Travel, PA, Bonds)






Mandatory: ALL vehicles on public roads MUST have motor insurance.
Minimum: Third-party coverage (Act Cover)
Penalties for Non-Compliance: - Fine: Up to RM1,000 - Imprisonment: Up to 3 months - Both fine AND imprisonment - License disqualification: 12 months
⚠️ EXAM ALERT: Motor insurance is COMPULSORY under RTA 1987.




FOUR Coverage Levels (MEMORIZE):









Coverage Type
What’s Covered
Premium
Common Use




1. Act Cover
Third-party death/injury ONLY
Lowest
Rarely written


2. Third Party
Act + Third-party property damage
Low
Budget option


3. Third Party Fire & Theft (TPFT)
Third Party + Own vehicle fire/theft
Medium
Mid-range


4. Comprehensive
All above + Own vehicle accident damage
Highest
Most complete




Detailed Comparison:
COVERAGE LEVELS (Lowest → Highest)

ACT COVER (Minimum Legal):
✅ Third-party death/bodily injury
❌ Third-party property damage
❌ Own vehicle damage
❌ Fire/theft

THIRD PARTY:
✅ Third-party death/injury
✅ Third-party property damage
❌ Own vehicle damage
❌ Fire/theft

THIRD PARTY FIRE & THEFT:
✅ All Third Party coverage
✅ Own vehicle fire damage
✅ Own vehicle theft
❌ Own vehicle accident damage

COMPREHENSIVE:
✅ All TPFT coverage
✅ Own vehicle accident damage
✅ Most complete protection
Example Scenarios:
Scenario 1: You hit another car
Third Party: Covers other car damage ✅
Comprehensive: Covers other car + YOUR car ✅

Scenario 2: Your car stolen
Third Party: NO coverage ❌
TPFT: Covers theft ✅
Comprehensive: Covers theft ✅

Scenario 3: You hit tree (own fault)
Third Party: NO coverage ❌
TPFT: NO coverage ❌
Comprehensive: Covers your car ✅
📌 EXAM TIP: Comprehensive = Everything covered; Third Party = Only others’ loss; TPFT = TP + Fire + Theft.




By Vehicle Type:



Type
Description
Example




Private Car
Personal/household use
Family sedan


Commercial Vehicle

Delivery van, taxi


Motorcycle

Motorbike, scooter


Motor Trade

Vehicles for sale/repair







Special Category: For Grab, Uber, etc.
Covers: - Enhanced liability (transporting passengers for hire) - Increased risks of passenger transport - Higher usage/mileage
Required: Cannot use personal car insurance for commercial e-hailing.




Definition: Discount for not making claims.
Accumulation: - Year 1 no claim: 25% NCD - Year 2 no claim: 30% NCD - Year 3 no claim: 38.33% NCD - Year 4 no claim: 45% NCD - Year 5+ no claim: 55% NCD (maximum)
Transfer: Can transfer NCD to new vehicle if same owner.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 10 (Links to Section 7.3.5 - NCD)
Question: “To capitalize on no claim discount for motor cover, the following must be performed: A. Increase in premium as mandated must be paid B. No claim discount applies beyond basic premium C. Evidence of entitlement from previous insurer must be obtained ✅ D. All the above”
Answer: C (Evidence of entitlement required)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Must PROVE NCD entitlement from previous insurer!
ANALYSIS:
C ✅ CORRECT: - Must obtain NCD certificate from previous insurer - Proves claim-free record - Required for NCD transfer - Cannot just claim verbally
Example:
Switching insurers:
Old Insurer: 3 years no claim (38.33% NCD)
New Insurer: Requires NCD certificate from old insurer
Without certificate: Start from 0% NCD
With certificate: Continue with 38.33% NCD
A ❌ Wrong: - NCD = DISCOUNT (reduces premium) - Not an increase in premium - Opposite concept
B ❌ Misleading: - NCD applies TO the premium (reduces it) - Not “beyond” basic premium - Unclear statement
KEYWORDS: - “Evidence of entitlement” = NCD certificate - “Previous insurer” = Transfer proof - “Must be obtained” = Required documentation
MEMORY TIP: “No Proof, No Discount” (need certificate)




Key Change: From tariffed rates to risk-based pricing.
Details: - Insurers can set own premiums based on risk assessment - Factors: Driving record, vehicle type, usage, location - Promotes competition - Encourages safe driving - Minimum premium: RM20 (still applicable for tariff products)




What’s NOT Covered: - Wear and tear - Mechanical/electrical breakdown - Driving under influence of alcohol/drugs - Unauthorized drivers - Use for illegal purposes - Negligent maintenance - Consequential losses







Five Main Types:

Fire and Special Perils
All Risk Insurance
Business Interruption/Consequential Loss
Houseowners Insurance
Burglary Insurance




Covers: - Fire damage - Lightning - Explosion/implosion - Aircraft damage - Impact by vehicles - Riot, strike, malicious damage
Excludes: - War, terrorism - Nuclear risks - Wear and tear - Consequential losses (lost profits)
Example:
Factory catches fire:
Building damage: RM500,000 ✅ Covered
Machinery damage: RM200,000 ✅ Covered
Lost profits (3 months): RM300,000 ❌ NOT covered (need Business Interruption)




Purpose: Cover lost profits due to property damage.
Covers: - Lost gross profit - Increased cost of working - Fixed costs continuing during interruption
Trigger: Must be property damage covered by underlying policy (e.g., fire).

📝 EXAM QUESTION 2 (Links to Section 7.4.A.III - Business Interruption)
Question: “Mr. Hew compensated when machine broke down. Amount covers loss of profits due to production interruption. What policy? A. Machinery Breakdown (Loss of Profit) Policy ✅ B. Fire (Consequential Loss) Policy C. Machinery & Equipment Policy D. Liability (Loss of Profit) Policy”
Answer: A (Machinery Breakdown Loss of Profit)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Loss of PROFITS from MACHINERY breakdown = Specific policy!
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ CORRECT: - Machinery Breakdown (Loss of Profit) Policy - Covers lost profits when machinery breaks down - Consequential loss from equipment failure - Exactly what question describes
B ❌ Wrong trigger: - Fire (Consequential Loss) = Lost profits from FIRE - Not machinery breakdown - Different peril
C ❌ Wrong coverage: - Machinery & Equipment = PHYSICAL damage to machine - Does NOT cover lost profits - Only repair/replacement costs
D ❌ No such policy: - Liability insurance covers legal liability to others - Not loss of profits from own machinery
POLICY MATCHING:
PHYSICAL Damage Coverage:
Machinery & Equipment Policy = Repair/replace machine

CONSEQUENTIAL Coverage (Lost Profits):
Machinery Breakdown (Loss of Profit) = Income loss from breakdown

Must have BOTH for complete protection!
KEYWORDS: - “Loss of profits” = Consequential coverage - “Machine broke down” = Machinery breakdown trigger - “Interruption of production” = Business interruption
MEMORY TIP: “Machine breaks → Profit lost → Loss of Profit Policy”




IMPORTANT DISTINCTION:



Aspect
Houseowners
Householders




Insured
Property OWNER
TENANT/Occupier


Building Coverage
✅ YES
❌ NO


Contents Coverage
✅ YES
✅ YES


Liability
✅ Owner’s liability
✅ Occupier’s liability



Example:
Mr. Lee OWNS house: Houseowners policy
- Building structure ✅
- Contents ✅
- Owner's liability ✅

Mr. Tan RENTS apartment: Householders policy
- Building ❌ (landlord's responsibility)
- Contents ✅
- Tenant's liability ✅





Purpose: Protect against legal liability to third parties.
Main Types:

Public Liability - General public/visitors
Product Liability - Defective products
Professional Indemnity - Professional errors
Directors & Officers (D&O) - Management decisions
Employer’s Liability - Employees (workplace accidents)
Workmen’s Compensation - Statutory coverage for workmen




Purpose: Cover employer’s legal liability for employee accidents.
What’s Covered: - Employer’s negligence - Breach of duty (safety measures) - Common law liability
What’s NOT Covered: - Employee’s own negligence (unless employer also negligent) - Statutory liability under Workmen’s Compensation Act

📝 EXAM QUESTION 7 (Links to Section 7.4.D.VI - Employer’s Liability)
Question: “Which falls under Employer’s Liability Policy? Employer’s liability for accidents to employee from: i. Employer’s personal negligence ii. Employer’s breach of duty (safety measures) iii. Employee’s own negligence
A. I only B. II only C. I & II only ✅ D. I & III only”
Answer: C (I & II only)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Employer’s Liability covers EMPLOYER’S fault, not employee’s own negligence!
ANALYSIS:
i. Employer’s personal negligence ✅ COVERED: - Employer failed to supervise properly - Employer gave unsafe instructions - Employer’s direct actions caused accident - EMPLOYER AT FAULT
ii. Employer’s breach of duty (safety) ✅ COVERED: - Failed to provide safe working environment - Inadequate safety equipment - No safety training - Poor maintenance - EMPLOYER FAILED DUTY OF CARE
iii. Employee’s own negligence ❌ NOT COVERED: - Employee was careless - Employee ignored safety rules - Employee’s own fault - NO EMPLOYER LIABILITY (employee responsible)
PRINCIPLE:
Employer's Liability Insurance:
Covers: Employer's FAULT ✅
Does NOT cover: Employee's FAULT ❌

Rationale: Employer only liable when employer at fault
EXAMPLE SCENARIOS:
Scenario 1: ✅ COVERED
Worker falls from height
Reason: Employer didn't provide safety harness
Result: EMPLOYER'S breach of duty (covered)

Scenario 2: ✅ COVERED
Worker injured by faulty machine
Reason: Employer failed to maintain equipment
Result: EMPLOYER'S negligence (covered)

Scenario 3: ❌ NOT COVERED
Worker ignores warning signs, gets injured
Reason: Worker's own negligence
No employer breach of duty
Result: NOT covered (employee at fault)
KEYWORDS: - “Employer’s negligence” = Employer at fault ✅ - “Employer’s breach of duty” = Employer failed obligation ✅ - “Employee’s own negligence” = Employee at fault ❌
MEMORY TIP: “Employer’s Liability = Employer’s FAULT only”




Legal Requirement: Employers MUST cover “workmen” without SOCSO.
Purpose: Statutory compensation for workplace injuries.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 6 (Links to Section 7.4.D.VII - Workmen’s Compensation)
Question: “Which TRUE under Workmen’s Compensation Policy as according to law? A. Employer must cover employees classified as ‘workmen’ and without SOCSO ✅ B. Employer must cover employees with SOCSO C. No legal requirement to cover workmen D. Fixed amount to cover all workmen”
Answer: A (Workmen without SOCSO must be covered)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Workmen’s Compensation is for employees NOT covered by SOCSO!
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ CORRECT: - Employers MUST insure “workmen” - BUT: Only if NOT covered by SOCSO - Two separate systems: - SOCSO = Social security (most employees) - Workmen’s Comp = Insurance (workmen not in SOCSO)
WHO ARE “WORKMEN”?: - Manual laborers - Certain categories of workers - Earning below specified amount - NOT covered by SOCSO
B ❌ Wrong - mutually exclusive: - If employee HAS SOCSO → NO Workmen’s Comp needed - SOCSO provides coverage already - Would be double coverage
C ❌ False - it IS required: - Workmen’s Compensation Act REQUIRES coverage - Legal obligation for employers - Penalties for non-compliance
D ❌ Not fixed amount: - Coverage varies by wages, risk category - Not a fixed amount for all
COVERAGE FRAMEWORK:
Employee Categories:

SOCSO-covered employees:
→ Protected by SOCSO ✅
→ NO Workmen's Comp needed ❌

"Workmen" without SOCSO:
→ NOT protected by SOCSO ❌
→ MUST have Workmen's Comp ✅

Purpose: Ensure ALL employees protected
KEYWORDS: - “Workmen” = Specific employee category - “Without SOCSO” = Gap that needs filling - “Must cover” = Legal requirement
MEMORY TIP: “No SOCSO → Need Workmen’s Comp” (ensure protection)





Three Main Types:

Contractor’s All Risks (CAR)
Erection All Risks (EAR)
Machinery Breakdown




Purpose: Protect construction projects during building phase.
Covers: - Construction works - Materials on site - Equipment used - Third-party liability
Typical Projects: Buildings, bridges, roads, tunnels.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 1 (Links to Section 7.4.E.I - CAR Insurance)
Question: “Mr. Kanesan asks for policy covering faulty design/construction of machines and damage during installation. Which suitable? A. Machinery Breakdown Policy B. Contractor’s All Risks Policy ✅ C. Comprehensive Machine Policy D. Loss of Profit policy”
Answer: B (Contractor’s All Risks)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: During INSTALLATION = Construction phase = CAR policy!
ANALYSIS:
B ✅ CORRECT - CAR Policy: - “During installation” = Construction/erection phase ✅ - “Faulty design/construction” = Construction risks ✅ - Covers work in progress - Includes installation damage
A ❌ Machinery Breakdown: - For OPERATIONAL machines (after installation) - Not during installation/construction - Wrong phase
C ❌ Comprehensive Machine: - For machines IN USE (operational) - Not installation phase - Wrong coverage period
D ❌ Loss of Profit: - Consequential loss (lost income) - Not physical damage during construction - Wrong coverage type
PHASE MATCHING:
CONSTRUCTION PHASE (installing/building):
→ Contractor's All Risks (CAR) ✅
→ Erection All Risks (EAR) ✅

OPERATIONAL PHASE (after installed, in use):
→ Machinery Breakdown ✅
→ Machinery & Equipment ✅

CONSEQUENTIAL (lost profits):
→ Loss of Profit policies ✅
KEYWORDS: - “Damage during installation” = Construction phase - “Faulty design/construction” = CAR coverage - “Machines” = Could be EAR too, but CAR covers broader construction
MEMORY TIP: “Installing = CAR/EAR; Operating = Machinery policies”

📝 EXAM QUESTION 8 (Links to Section 7.4.E - CAR Exclusions)
Question: “Key exclusions of Contractor’s All Risk Policy: i. Loss due to war ii. Loss due to wilful act of insured iii. Loss due to nuclear radiation
A. I only B. I & II only C. I & III only D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: CAR excludes WAR, WILFUL ACTS, and NUCLEAR risks!
ANALYSIS:
i. War ✅ EXCLUDED: - War, invasion, civil war - Uninsurable risk (catastrophic) - Standard exclusion all policies
ii. Wilful act of insured ✅ EXCLUDED: - Intentional damage by insured - Fraud prevention - Moral hazard control - Cannot profit from own wrongdoing
iii. Nuclear radiation ✅ EXCLUDED: - Nuclear incident, radioactive contamination - Catastrophic risk - Uninsurable - Standard exclusion
COMMON EXCLUSIONS IN GENERAL INSURANCE:
Almost ALL general insurance excludes:
❌ War and war-like operations
❌ Nuclear risks
❌ Intentional acts by insured
❌ Wear and tear
❌ Inherent vice

These are STANDARD exclusions
KEYWORDS: - “War” = Catastrophic, uninsurable - “Wilful act” = Intentional damage (moral hazard) - “Nuclear” = Catastrophic risk
MEMORY TIP: “WON’T cover War, Own Acts, Nuclear” (WON acronym)




Purpose: Cover installation/erection of machinery and equipment.
Covers: - Installation of plant and machinery - Testing and commissioning - Damage during erection - Third-party liability
Difference from CAR: EAR = Machinery installation; CAR = Building construction.





Definition: Guarantee that party will fulfill contractual obligations.
Three Main Construction Bonds (MEMORIZE):

Tender Bond
Performance Bond
Advance Payment Bond


📝 EXAM QUESTION 3, 4, 5 (Links to Section 7.4.F - Bonds)
Question 3: “Which NOT a type of bond in construction? A. Tender Bond B. Performance C. Banking Security Bond ✅ D. Advance Payment Bond”
Answer: C (Banking Security Bond - NOT construction bond)
Question 4: “Which bond required for submission of tenders? A. Tender Bond ✅ B. Performance C. Banking Security Bond D. Advance Payment Bond”
Answer: A (Tender Bond)
Question 5: “Which bond ensures contractor fulfills duties within specified period? A. Tender Bond B. Performance ✅ C. Banking Security Bond D. Advance Payment Bond”
Answer: B (Performance Bond)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: THREE construction bonds - Tender, Performance, Advance Payment!

COMPREHENSIVE BOND ANALYSIS:
1. TENDER BOND (Question 4):
Purpose: Guarantee bidder will honor tender if accepted.
When Required: Submission of tender/bid for contract.
Protects: Project owner (principal) against contractor backing out.
Amount: Usually 2-5% of tender value.
Example:
Company submits tender for RM10 million project
Tender Bond: RM200,000 (2%)

If company wins but backs out:
Principal keeps RM200,000 (compensates for wasted time/re-tendering)

2. PERFORMANCE BOND (Question 5):
Purpose: Ensure contractor completes project as specified.
When Required: After contract awarded, during project execution.
Protects: Owner against contractor default, delays, poor quality.
Amount: Usually 10% of contract value.
Example:
Building contract: RM10 million
Performance Bond: RM1 million (10%)

If contractor abandons project or fails to complete:
Owner claims RM1 million to hire another contractor

3. ADVANCE PAYMENT BOND:
Purpose: Guarantee refund if contractor doesn’t perform after receiving advance.
When Required: When contractor receives upfront payment.
Protects: Owner’s advance payment.
Amount: Usually equals advance payment amount.
Example:
Contract: RM10 million
Advance payment: RM2 million (20%)
Advance Payment Bond: RM2 million

If contractor takes money and doesn't work:
Owner claims RM2 million back from bond

4. BANKING SECURITY BOND (Question 3) - ❌ NOT A CONSTRUCTION BOND: - NOT specific to construction industry - General banking/financial guarantee - WRONG ANSWER (this is the trap!)

BOND SEQUENCE IN PROJECT:
PROJECT LIFECYCLE:

STEP 1: Tendering
→ TENDER BOND (ensure serious bidders)

STEP 2: Contract Award
→ PERFORMANCE BOND (ensure completion)
→ ADVANCE PAYMENT BOND (if advance given)

STEP 3: Project Execution
→ Bonds remain active until completion

STEP 4: Completion
→ Bonds released
KEYWORDS: - “Tender” = Bidding stage - “Performance” = Execution/completion - “Advance Payment” = Protect upfront payment - “Banking Security” = NOT construction bond
MEMORY TIP:
TAP for Construction:
T = Tender Bond (bidding)
A = Advance Payment Bond (upfront $)
P = Performance Bond (completion)




Other Types: - Money Insurance (cash in transit) - Fidelity Guarantee (employee dishonesty) - Plate Glass Insurance - Electronic Equipment Insurance - Cyber Insurance (data breach, cyber attacks)





Personal Accident (PA) Insurance
Medical Insurance (covered in Chapter 5)
Travel Insurance






📝 EXAM QUESTION 9 (Links to Section 7.3 - Motor Insurance Rules)
Question: “Rules governing motor insurance Malaysia. Identify correct: i. No official receipt required ii. Post-dated cheques can be accepted iii. Premiums received within 7 days from risk commences
A. I & II only B. I, II & III only C. I & IV only D. All the above”
Answer: C (Wait - seems error in question, “IV” not listed)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Cash Before Cover principle - payment BEFORE coverage starts!
CORRECT RULES:
Cash Before Cover Principle: - Premium must be paid BEFORE coverage starts - Official receipt MUST be issued - Post-dated cheques generally NOT accepted (payment must clear) - No credit extended
LIKELY ANSWER: Based on standard practice, proper rules are: - Official receipt IS required ✅ - Post-dated cheques NOT accepted ❌ - Premium paid BEFORE cover (not after 7 days) ✅
Note: Question may have formatting error. Standard rule = “Cash before cover, no credit”.

title: Chapter 7: General Insurance Products in Insurance Planning
text:
GENERAL INSURANCE ESSENTIALS

PRINCIPLES:
Indemnity - Restore original position
Contribution - Share among insurers
Subrogation - Recover from third party

MOTOR LEVELS:
Act < Third Party < TPFT < Comprehensive

CONSTRUCTION BONDS (TAP):
Tender - Bidding
Advance Payment - Upfront $
Performance - Completion

PHASE MATCHING:
Installation → CAR/EAR
Operation → Machinery Breakdown
Lost Profit → Consequential Loss

EMPLOYER LIABILITY:
Covers: Employer's fault
NOT: Employee's own negligence

WORKMEN'S COMP:
Only for workmen WITHOUT SOCSO

END OF CHAPTER 7 STUDY GUIDE
General Insurance: Protect Assets, Manage Liability, Ensure Business Continuity!

title: Chapter 11: SOCSO (Social Security Organization)
text:
SOCSO (Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial - PERKESO) is Malaysia’s social security system providing protection to employees against work-related and non-work-related injuries, disabilities, and death. Understanding SOCSO is essential for comprehensive financial planning.
Exam Weight: 5-7% of total exam
Study Time Recommendation: 4-5 hours




By the end of this chapter, you must be able to:

Explain SOCSO’s role and importance in Malaysia’s social safety net
Identify eligibility criteria for SOCSO schemes
Distinguish between Employment Injury and Invalidity Pension schemes
Calculate contribution rates for employers and employees
Understand definitions of wages for contribution purposes
Know employer and employee responsibilities
Identify benefits under each scheme
Understand appeals process







Full Name: - English: Social Security Organization (SOCSO) - Malay: Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (PERKESO)
Established: - Act: Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 - Operations began: 1971
Primary Mission: Provide financial aid and support to employees and dependents in case of: - Work-related injuries - Disabilities - Illnesses - Death




CRITICAL FRAMEWORK (HIGH EXAM FREQUENCY):
SOCSO TWO SCHEMES
├── 1. Employment Injury Insurance Scheme (EIIS)
│   └── Work-related injuries and diseases
└── 2. Invalidity Pension Scheme (IPS)
    └── Non-work-related disabilities and death



Coverage: - Work-related injuries or diseases - Commuting accidents (to/from work) - Accidents during working hours
Key Features:



Feature
Details




Age Limit
NO age limit


Eligibility
All registered SOCSO employees


Type of Incidents
Work-related only


Coverage Period
As long as employed and contributing



Benefits Provided: - Medical treatment - Temporary disablement benefit - Permanent disablement benefit - Dependents’ benefit (if death) - Funeral benefit - Rehabilitation services - Education benefit for children

📝 EXAM QUESTION 6 (Links to Section 11.5 - EIIS Coverage)
Question: “Employment Injury Insurance Scheme covers: I. Diseases contracted due to work environment exposure II. Accidents at workplace but employee not on duty III. Accidents while out for lunch during break time
A. I and II B. II and III C. I and III ✅ D. None of the above”
Answer: C (I and III)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: EIIS covers WORK-RELATED incidents + reasonable work activities (including lunch breaks)!
DETAILED ANALYSIS:
I. Diseases from work environment exposure ✅ COVERED: - Occupational diseases are covered - Examples: Asbestosis (construction), Silicosis (mining), Chemical poisoning - Must be contracted due to work exposure - Established causal link to work environment
Example:
Factory worker exposed to toxic chemicals
Develops respiratory disease over 5 years
Medical evidence links disease to workplace exposure
Result: EIIS COVERS treatment and disability benefits
II. Accidents at workplace BUT not on duty ❌ NOT COVERED: - Key phrase: “Not on duty” - At workplace but NOT working = NOT covered - Must be performing work duties or work-related activity
Example:
Employee stays after hours for personal reasons
Not working, just using office Wi-Fi for personal matters
Gets injured (e.g., falls down stairs)
Result: NOT COVERED (not on duty)
III. Accidents during lunch break ✅ COVERED: - Lunch break = REASONABLE WORK ACTIVITY - Part of normal work day - Even if off premises (going to nearby restaurant) - Commuting principle extends to lunch travel
Example:
Employee goes to nearby restaurant during lunch hour
Gets into accident crossing road
Result: COVERED (lunch break is work-related activity)
COVERAGE PRINCIPLE:
COVERED:
✅ While performing work duties
✅ Commuting to/from work
✅ During reasonable work breaks (lunch, tea)
✅ Work-related travel
✅ Occupational diseases

NOT COVERED:
❌ Personal activities at workplace (not on duty)
❌ Non-work-related incidents
❌ Intentional self-harm
KEYWORDS: - “Work environment exposure” = Occupational disease ✅ - “Not on duty” = Personal time ❌ - “Lunch during break time” = Work-related activity ✅
MEMORY TIP: “Working Hours + Work-Related = Covered” (including reasonable breaks)




Coverage: - Non-work-related long-term illness or disability - Death due to any cause (work or non-work) - Permanent incapacity
Key Features:







Feature
Details




Age Limit
Must be UNDER 60 at time of diagnosis


Eligibility
All registered SOCSO employees


Type of Incidents
Non-work-related disabilities/death


Medical Requirement
Medical board certification of permanent incapacity



Benefits Provided: - Invalidity pension (monthly payments) - Constant attendance allowance (for severely disabled) - Survivors’ pension (for dependents if death) - Funeral benefit - Education benefit for dependent children

📝 EXAM QUESTION 7 (Links to Section 11.6 - IPS Benefits)
Question: “Under Invalidity Pension Scheme, employee/dependents receive: I. Invalidity pension II. Constant attendance allowance III. Education loan for dependent children
A. I and II B. II and III C. I and III D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: IPS provides COMPREHENSIVE support - all three benefits available!
BENEFIT ANALYSIS:
I. Invalidity Pension ✅ PROVIDED: - Monthly pension for permanently disabled employee - Continues for life (as long as disability persists) - Amount based on contribution history and degree of disability - Replaces lost income
Example:
Employee suffers stroke (non-work-related)
Medical board certifies permanent 60% disability
Cannot work anymore
Receives: Monthly invalidity pension (e.g., RM1,500/month for life)
II. Constant Attendance Allowance ✅ PROVIDED: - For SEVERELY disabled requiring constant care - Additional monthly payment beyond pension - Recognizes extra care costs - Helps family cope with caregiving burden
Example:
Employee permanently bedridden after accident
Requires 24/7 care for basic needs (feeding, bathing, etc.)
Receives: Invalidity pension + Constant attendance allowance
(e.g., RM1,500 pension + RM500 attendance = RM2,000/month)
III. Education Benefit for Dependent Children ✅ PROVIDED: - NOT loan, but BENEFIT (no repayment needed!) - For dependent children’s education - Helps family maintain children’s schooling - Continues even after employee’s death
Example:
Disabled employee has 2 children (age 10 and 12)
Both in school
SOCSO provides: Education benefit to support their studies
Ensures children can continue education despite family hardship
IMPORTANT NOTE:
Question says "Education LOAN"
Actually: Education BENEFIT (grant, not loan)
But answer still D - all three types of support provided
Don't get tricked by wording!
COMPREHENSIVE IPS BENEFITS: 1. ✅ Invalidity Pension (monthly income) 2. ✅ Constant Attendance Allowance (for severe cases) 3. ✅ Survivors’ Pension (if employee dies) 4. ✅ Funeral Benefit 5. ✅ Education Benefit (for children)
KEYWORDS: - “Invalidity pension” = Monthly payment for disability - “Constant attendance” = Extra for severe disability - “Education benefit” = Support for children (not loan) - “All the above” = Comprehensive coverage
MEMORY TIP: “IPS = Income + Care + Education” (complete family support)





Who is COVERED: - ✅ Permanent employees - ✅ Temporary employees - ✅ Casual workers - ✅ Part-time workers - ✅ Contract workers - ✅ All wage levels (no minimum/maximum)
Who is EXCLUDED (CRITICAL - HIGH EXAM FREQUENCY):



Excluded Category
Reason




Self-employed persons
No employer-employee relationship


Domestic workers
Special category, separate scheme


Government servants
Covered by government pension scheme


Foreign workers
Some voluntary coverage provisions




📝 EXAM QUESTION 2 (Links to Section 11.3 - Eligibility)
Question: “Which categories exempted from SOCSO? I. Self-employed persons II. Government servants III. Contract workers
A. I and II ✅ B. II and III C. I and III D. All the above”
Answer: A (I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Self-employed and Government servants exempted; Contract workers are COVERED!
ANALYSIS:
I. Self-employed persons ✅ EXEMPTED: - Run own business - No employer - BUT: Can join Self-Employment Social Security Scheme (voluntary) - Not automatically covered under SOCSO
II. Government servants ✅ EXEMPTED: - Government employees - Covered by government pension scheme instead - Different social security system - Federal, state, local government workers
III. Contract workers ❌ NOT EXEMPTED (ARE COVERED): - COVERED under SOCSO! - As long as employer-employee relationship exists - Employed under contract of service - Must be registered and contribute
COMMON TRAP:
Students think: "Contract" = Temporary = Exempted
REALITY: Contract workers = COVERED
KEY DISTINCTION:
EXEMPTED:
- Self-employed (NO employer)
- Government servants (Different scheme)
- Domestic workers (Special category)
- Foreign workers (Generally)

COVERED:
- Permanent workers ✅
- Temporary workers ✅
- Casual workers ✅
- Part-time workers ✅
- CONTRACT WORKERS ✅ (Don't confuse!)
KEYWORDS: - “Self-employed” = Exempted (no employer) - “Government servants” = Exempted (different scheme) - “Contract workers” = COVERED (employed!)
MEMORY TIP: “SGDF Out, Workers In” (Self/Govt/Domestic/Foreign out; all workers in)




CRITICAL NUMBERS (MUST MEMORIZE):



Party
Rate
Based On




Employee
0.5%
Monthly wages


Employer
1.75%
Monthly wages


Total
2.25%
Monthly wages



⚠️ EXAM ALERT: Most common question - memorize 0.5% (employee) and 1.75% (employer)!

📝 EXAM QUESTION 3 (Links to Section 11.4 - Contribution Rates)
Question: “What are contribution rates by employees and employers? A. Employees 0.5% and employers 1.75% ✅ B. Employees 0.75% and employers 1.50% C. Employees 0.5% and employers 1.50% D. Employees 0.75% and employers 1.75%”
Answer: A (Employee 0.5%, Employer 1.75%)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: 0.5% + 1.75% = 2.25% total - Employee pays LESS, Employer pays MORE!
MEMORIZATION TABLE:




Employee
Employer
Total




Rate
0.5%
1.75%
2.25%


Ratio
1 part
3.5 parts
4.5 parts



CALCULATION EXAMPLE:
Employee Monthly Salary: RM3,000

Employee Contribution:
RM3,000 × 0.5% = RM15

Employer Contribution:
RM3,000 × 1.75% = RM52.50

Total to SOCSO:
RM15 + RM52.50 = RM67.50
WHY THESE RATES?: - Employee bears SMALLER burden (0.5%) - Employer bears LARGER burden (1.75%) - Employer responsible for employee welfare - Social security shared responsibility
COMMON EXAM TRAPS:
❌ Trap 1: Confusing rates
Wrong: 0.75% employee (EPF rate confusion)
Right: 0.5% employee
❌ Trap 2: Equal sharing
Wrong: Both pay 1.125% (equal)
Right: 0.5% + 1.75% (unequal)
❌ Trap 3: Reversed rates
Wrong: Employee 1.75%, Employer 0.5%
Right: Employee 0.5%, Employer 1.75%
KEYWORDS: - “0.5%” = Employee (smaller) - “1.75%” = Employer (larger) - “Monthly wages” = Contribution base
MEMORY TRICK:
"HALF percent for EMPLOYEE" (0.5%)
"Almost TWO percent for EMPLOYER" (1.75%)
VISUAL MEMORY:
Employee: 0.5% = 🪙 (small coin)
Employer: 1.75% = 🪙🪙🪙 (multiple coins - more than 3x employee)




What is INCLUDED in “Wages”: - ✅ Basic salary - ✅ Allowances (housing, transport, etc.) - ✅ Commissions - ✅ Overtime pay - ✅ Payments for leave (annual leave, sick leave)
What is EXCLUDED from “Wages”:







Excluded Item
Reason




Annual bonus
One-time payment, not regular wages


Employer’s contribution to statutory funds
Employer’s separate obligation (EPF, SOCSO)


Service charge/tips
Not guaranteed, variable


Gratuity
Retirement payment


Retrenchment compensation
Termination payment




📝 EXAM QUESTION 5 (Links to Section 11.5 - Wages Definition)
Question: “Which payments NOT considered wages for SOCSO? I. Annual bonus II. Employer’s contribution to statutory fund III. Payments for leave
A. I and II ✅ B. II and III C. I and III D. None of the above”
Answer: A (I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Regular payments = Wages; One-time/Statutory = NOT wages!
DETAILED ANALYSIS:
I. Annual Bonus ✅ NOT WAGES: - One-time annual payment - Not regular monthly income - Discretionary (not guaranteed) - EXCLUDED from SOCSO contribution calculation
Example:
Employee Monthly Salary: RM3,000
Annual Bonus: RM6,000 (2 months)

SOCSO Contribution Based On:
Monthly: RM3,000 only (NOT RM3,000 + RM500 bonus portion)
II. Employer’s Contribution to Statutory Fund ✅ NOT WAGES: - Employer’s separate legal obligation - Examples: EPF contribution, SOCSO contribution itself - NOT part of employee’s wages - Already separate line item
Example:
Employee Salary: RM3,000
Employer EPF: RM390 (13%)
Employer SOCSO: RM52.50 (1.75%)

Wages for SOCSO calculation: RM3,000 only
(NOT RM3,000 + RM390 + RM52.50)
III. Payments for Leave ❌ IS WAGES (INCLUDED): - Regular income replacement - Annual leave pay, sick leave pay - Part of normal employment terms - INCLUDED in wages calculation
Example:
Employee takes 5 days annual leave
Receives: RM500 leave pay

This RM500 IS included in wages for SOCSO
Contributes: RM500 × 0.5% = RM2.50
WAGES DETERMINATION PRINCIPLE:
INCLUDED (IS Wages):
✅ Regular monthly payments
✅ Guaranteed employment income
✅ Salary, allowances, overtime
✅ Leave payments
✅ Commissions

EXCLUDED (NOT Wages):
❌ One-time bonuses
❌ Employer's statutory contributions
❌ Gratuity/retirement payments
❌ Retrenchment compensation
❌ Tips/service charges (variable)
WHY THIS MATTERS: - Affects contribution calculation - Higher “wages” = Higher contribution - Must know what to include/exclude - Compliance requirement
KEYWORDS: - “Annual bonus” = One-time, NOT wages - “Statutory fund contribution” = Separate, NOT wages - “Leave payments” = Regular, IS wages
MEMORY TIP: “Regular = Wages, One-time = Not Wages”




TWO Types of Employers (CRITICAL):


Definition: - Employer who directly employs the employee - Undertakes payment of wages - Handles all service matters (HR, administration)
Example:
ABC Manufacturing Sdn Bhd
↓ (directly hires)
Factory Worker
↓
ABC pays salary, manages employment
Result: ABC = Principal Employer




Definition: - Contractor/subcontractor who directly supervises work - May not pay wages (principal employer pays) - Employee works under immediate employer’s supervision
Example:
ABC Company (Principal Employer)
↓ (contracts to)
XYZ Contractor (Immediate Employer)
↓ (supervises)
Worker on site
↓
Worker physically works for XYZ
But ABC pays wages

📝 EXAM QUESTION 9 & 10 (Links to Section 11.6 - Employer Types)
Question 9: “Employers under SOCSO categorized into: I. Principal employer II. Immediate employer
A. I only B. II only C. I and II only ✅ D. Neither I nor II”
Answer: C (Both I and II)
Question 10: “Principal Employer refers to: I. Employer who employed employee directly II. Employer who undertakes payment of wages and service matters
A. I only B. II only C. I and II only ✅ D. Neither I nor II”
Answer: C (Both I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: TWO employer types exist; Principal = Direct employment + Wages/Service responsibility!
COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS:
Question 9 - Two Categories: Both categories exist in SOCSO framework: - Principal Employer: Main employer (direct employment, pays wages) - Immediate Employer: On-site supervisor (may be contractor)
Question 10 - Principal Employer Definition: BOTH statements define Principal Employer:
I. Direct Employment ✅: - Hired employee directly - Employment contract with principal - Not through intermediary
II. Payment & Service Matters ✅: - Pays wages to employee - Handles HR administration - Manages employment relationship - Responsible for benefits, leave, etc.
RELATIONSHIP DIAGRAM:
Typical Scenario:

(Main Company)

IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER
(Contractor/Supervisor)
    ├── Supervises work day-to-day
    ├── May not pay wages
    └── On-site management
PRACTICAL EXAMPLE:
Construction Project:

ABC Developer (Principal Employer):
- Hires construction workers
- Pays monthly salaries
- Manages HR, benefits
- Registers with SOCSO

XYZ Contractor (Immediate Employer):
- Supervises workers on site
- Directs daily work
- Reports to principal
- NOT responsible for SOCSO

PRINCIPAL = PAYS (wages + contributions)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 4 (Links to Section 11.7 - SOCSO Key Facts)
Question: “Which TRUE for SOCSO? I. Scheme compulsory except for exempted workers II. If have SOCSO + other insurance, can only claim from one III. After age 60, can still be covered if employer contributes
A. I and II B. II and III C. I and III D. None of the above ✅”
Answer: D (None of the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Statement II and III are FALSE - only Statement I is true, but “None” means all must be true!
STATEMENT ANALYSIS:
I. Scheme compulsory except exempted workers ✅ TRUE: - SOCSO is MANDATORY for eligible workers - Exemptions: Self-employed, government servants, domestic workers, foreign workers - Not optional for covered employees
II. Can only claim from one scheme ❌ FALSE: - Can claim from BOTH SOCSO AND other insurance! - SOCSO is SOCIAL SECURITY, not insurance exclusion - Other insurance (life, PA, medical) INDEPENDENT - Can claim medical from SOCSO + medical insurance - Can receive SOCSO pension + life insurance payout
Example:
Worker injured at work (EIIS coverage):

From SOCSO:
- Medical treatment (free)
- Temporary disablement benefit (RM2,000/month)
- Rehabilitation

From Personal Accident Insurance:
- RM50,000 lump sum payout
- Medical expense reimbursement

Result: CAN CLAIM FROM BOTH! ✅
III. After age 60, can be covered if employer contributes ❌ FALSE: - INVALIDITY scheme: Must be UNDER 60 at diagnosis - EMPLOYMENT INJURY scheme: No age limit for NEW injuries - BUT: Once reach 60, STOP contributing to Invalidity Scheme - NEW employees aged 60+ = Only Employment Injury coverage
Correct Rule:
Employee aged 58:
- Contributes to BOTH schemes ✅

Employee turns 60:
- STOPS contributing to Invalidity Scheme ❌
- CONTINUES Employment Injury coverage only ✅

Employee hired at age 62:
- Only Employment Injury coverage ✅
- NO Invalidity Scheme coverage ❌
WHY “NONE OF THE ABOVE”?: - Statement I: TRUE ✅ - Statement II: FALSE ❌ - Statement III: FALSE ❌ - Question asks which are TRUE - Only I is true, but answer options require multiple true statements - Since II and III are false, answer = None of the above
KEYWORDS: - “Compulsory” = Mandatory (TRUE) - “Only claim from one” = FALSE (can claim multiple) - “After 60 coverage” = FALSE (Invalidity stops at 60)
MEMORY TIP: “SOCSO + Insurance = Both Okay!” (not mutually exclusive)




📝 EXAM QUESTION 1 (Links to Section 11.2 - Mission)
Question: “SOCSO mission statements, which correct? I. Promote work safety/health of workers II. Promote work safety/health of employers III. Strengthen fund through contribution rate review
A. I and II ✅ B. II and III C. I and III D. All the above”
Answer: A (I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Mission focuses on SAFETY promotion (workers AND employers), NOT fund strengthening!
ANALYSIS:
I. Promote work safety/health of WORKERS ✅ MISSION: - Core SOCSO objective - Prevent workplace injuries - Protect employee welfare - Education and awareness programs
II. Promote work safety/health of EMPLOYERS ✅ MISSION: - Encourage safer workplaces - Employer education programs - Incentivize safety compliance - Reduce overall claims
III. Strengthen fund through contribution review ❌ NOT MISSION: - This is OPERATIONAL STRATEGY, not mission - Mission = Social welfare goals - Fund management = Implementation method - Contribution rates = Technical matter
DISTINCTION:
MISSION (What we aim to achieve):
✅ Worker safety and health
✅ Employer safety promotion
✅ Social security protection
✅ Rehabilitation services

STRATEGIES (How we achieve it):
- Fund management
- Contribution rate setting
- Technology adoption
- Service delivery improvement
KEYWORDS: - “Mission” = Core purpose - “Promote safety/health” = Protection objective - “Strengthen fund” = Strategy, not mission




📝 EXAM QUESTION 8 (Links to Section 11.9 - Appeals)
Question: “If employer/employee/dependents not satisfied with SOCSO decision, appeal to: A. SOCSO Board B. Social Security Appellate Board ✅ C. Medical and Hospital Appeal Board D. Social Security Appellate Board” (Note: B and D same - likely typo in original)
Answer: B or D (Social Security Appellate Board)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Appeals go to INDEPENDENT Appellate Board, NOT internal SOCSO Board!
APPEALS STRUCTURE:
STEP 1: SOCSO Decision (claim approval/rejection)
    ↓ (if not satisfied)
STEP 2: Appeal to Social Security Appellate Board
    ↓ (independent review)
STEP 3: Binding Decision
WHY APPELLATE BOARD?: - Independent body (not SOCSO internal) - Ensures fair review - Legal expertise - Quasi-judicial function
KEYWORDS: - “Appeal” = Challenge decision - “Appellate Board” = Independent review body - NOT “SOCSO Board” (internal)







1. Two Main Schemes: - EIIS - Employment Injury Insurance Scheme (work-related) - IPS - Invalidity Pension Scheme (non-work-related)
2. Contribution Rates: - Employee: 0.5% - Employer: 1.75% - Total: 2.25%
3. Exempted Categories: - Self-employed persons - Government servants - Domestic workers - Foreign workers (generally)
4. Age Limits: - EIIS: NO age limit - IPS: Must be UNDER 60 at diagnosis

7. Wages Exclude: - Annual bonus, employer statutory contributions
8. IPS Benefits: - Invalidity pension - Constant attendance allowance - Education benefit for children - Survivors’ pension - Funeral benefit
9. Appeals: - To Social Security Appellate Board (not SOCSO Board)

title: Chapter 11: SOCSO (Social Security Organization)
text:
Full Name: - English: Social Security Organization (SOCSO) - Malay: Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (PERKESO)
Established: - Act: Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 - Operations began: 1971
Primary Mission: Provide financial aid and support to employees and dependents in case of: - Work-related injuries - Disabilities - Illnesses - Death




CRITICAL FRAMEWORK (HIGH EXAM FREQUENCY):
SOCSO TWO SCHEMES
├── 1. Employment Injury Insurance Scheme (EIIS)
│   └── Work-related injuries and diseases
└── 2. Invalidity Pension Scheme (IPS)
    └── Non-work-related disabilities and death



Coverage: - Work-related injuries or diseases - Commuting accidents (to/from work) - Accidents during working hours
Key Features:



Feature
Details




Age Limit
NO age limit


Eligibility
All registered SOCSO employees


Type of Incidents
Work-related only


Coverage Period
As long as employed and contributing



Benefits Provided: - Medical treatment - Temporary disablement benefit - Permanent disablement benefit - Dependents’ benefit (if death) - Funeral benefit - Rehabilitation services - Education benefit for children

📝 EXAM QUESTION 6 (Links to Section 11.5 - EIIS Coverage)
Question: “Employment Injury Insurance Scheme covers: I. Diseases contracted due to work environment exposure II. Accidents at workplace but employee not on duty III. Accidents while out for lunch during break time
A. I and II B. II and III C. I and III ✅ D. None of the above”
Answer: C (I and III)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: EIIS covers WORK-RELATED incidents + reasonable work activities (including lunch breaks)!
DETAILED ANALYSIS:
I. Diseases from work environment exposure ✅ COVERED: - Occupational diseases are covered - Examples: Asbestosis (construction), Silicosis (mining), Chemical poisoning - Must be contracted due to work exposure - Established causal link to work environment
Example:
Factory worker exposed to toxic chemicals
Develops respiratory disease over 5 years
Medical evidence links disease to workplace exposure
Result: EIIS COVERS treatment and disability benefits
II. Accidents at workplace BUT not on duty ❌ NOT COVERED: - Key phrase: “Not on duty” - At workplace but NOT working = NOT covered - Must be performing work duties or work-related activity
Example:
Employee stays after hours for personal reasons
Not working, just using office Wi-Fi for personal matters
Gets injured (e.g., falls down stairs)
Result: NOT COVERED (not on duty)
III. Accidents during lunch break ✅ COVERED: - Lunch break = REASONABLE WORK ACTIVITY - Part of normal work day - Even if off premises (going to nearby restaurant) - Commuting principle extends to lunch travel
Example:
Employee goes to nearby restaurant during lunch hour
Gets into accident crossing road
Result: COVERED (lunch break is work-related activity)
COVERAGE PRINCIPLE:
COVERED:
✅ While performing work duties
✅ Commuting to/from work
✅ During reasonable work breaks (lunch, tea)
✅ Work-related travel
✅ Occupational diseases

NOT COVERED:
❌ Personal activities at workplace (not on duty)
❌ Non-work-related incidents
❌ Intentional self-harm
KEYWORDS: - “Work environment exposure” = Occupational disease ✅ - “Not on duty” = Personal time ❌ - “Lunch during break time” = Work-related activity ✅
MEMORY TIP: “Working Hours + Work-Related = Covered” (including reasonable breaks)




Coverage: - Non-work-related long-term illness or disability - Death due to any cause (work or non-work) - Permanent incapacity
Key Features:







Feature
Details




Age Limit
Must be UNDER 60 at time of diagnosis


Eligibility
All registered SOCSO employees


Type of Incidents
Non-work-related disabilities/death


Medical Requirement
Medical board certification of permanent incapacity



Benefits Provided: - Invalidity pension (monthly payments) - Constant attendance allowance (for severely disabled) - Survivors’ pension (for dependents if death) - Funeral benefit - Education benefit for dependent children

📝 EXAM QUESTION 7 (Links to Section 11.6 - IPS Benefits)
Question: “Under Invalidity Pension Scheme, employee/dependents receive: I. Invalidity pension II. Constant attendance allowance III. Education loan for dependent children
A. I and II B. II and III C. I and III D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: IPS provides COMPREHENSIVE support - all three benefits available!
BENEFIT ANALYSIS:
I. Invalidity Pension ✅ PROVIDED: - Monthly pension for permanently disabled employee - Continues for life (as long as disability persists) - Amount based on contribution history and degree of disability - Replaces lost income
Example:
Employee suffers stroke (non-work-related)
Medical board certifies permanent 60% disability
Cannot work anymore
Receives: Monthly invalidity pension (e.g., RM1,500/month for life)
II. Constant Attendance Allowance ✅ PROVIDED: - For SEVERELY disabled requiring constant care - Additional monthly payment beyond pension - Recognizes extra care costs - Helps family cope with caregiving burden
Example:
Employee permanently bedridden after accident
Requires 24/7 care for basic needs (feeding, bathing, etc.)
Receives: Invalidity pension + Constant attendance allowance
(e.g., RM1,500 pension + RM500 attendance = RM2,000/month)
III. Education Benefit for Dependent Children ✅ PROVIDED: - NOT loan, but BENEFIT (no repayment needed!) - For dependent children’s education - Helps family maintain children’s schooling - Continues even after employee’s death
Example:
Disabled employee has 2 children (age 10 and 12)
Both in school
SOCSO provides: Education benefit to support their studies
Ensures children can continue education despite family hardship
IMPORTANT NOTE:
Question says "Education LOAN"
Actually: Education BENEFIT (grant, not loan)
But answer still D - all three types of support provided
Don't get tricked by wording!
COMPREHENSIVE IPS BENEFITS: 1. ✅ Invalidity Pension (monthly income) 2. ✅ Constant Attendance Allowance (for severe cases) 3. ✅ Survivors’ Pension (if employee dies) 4. ✅ Funeral Benefit 5. ✅ Education Benefit (for children)
KEYWORDS: - “Invalidity pension” = Monthly payment for disability - “Constant attendance” = Extra for severe disability - “Education benefit” = Support for children (not loan) - “All the above” = Comprehensive coverage
MEMORY TIP: “IPS = Income + Care + Education” (complete family support)





Who is COVERED: - ✅ Permanent employees - ✅ Temporary employees - ✅ Casual workers - ✅ Part-time workers - ✅ Contract workers - ✅ All wage levels (no minimum/maximum)
Who is EXCLUDED (CRITICAL - HIGH EXAM FREQUENCY):



Excluded Category
Reason




Self-employed persons
No employer-employee relationship


Domestic workers
Special category, separate scheme


Government servants
Covered by government pension scheme


Foreign workers
Some voluntary coverage provisions




📝 EXAM QUESTION 2 (Links to Section 11.3 - Eligibility)
Question: “Which categories exempted from SOCSO? I. Self-employed persons II. Government servants III. Contract workers
A. I and II ✅ B. II and III C. I and III D. All the above”
Answer: A (I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Self-employed and Government servants exempted; Contract workers are COVERED!
ANALYSIS:
I. Self-employed persons ✅ EXEMPTED: - Run own business - No employer - BUT: Can join Self-Employment Social Security Scheme (voluntary) - Not automatically covered under SOCSO
II. Government servants ✅ EXEMPTED: - Government employees - Covered by government pension scheme instead - Different social security system - Federal, state, local government workers
III. Contract workers ❌ NOT EXEMPTED (ARE COVERED): - COVERED under SOCSO! - As long as employer-employee relationship exists - Employed under contract of service - Must be registered and contribute
COMMON TRAP:
Students think: "Contract" = Temporary = Exempted
REALITY: Contract workers = COVERED
KEY DISTINCTION:
EXEMPTED:
- Self-employed (NO employer)
- Government servants (Different scheme)
- Domestic workers (Special category)

COVERED:
- Permanent workers ✅
- Temporary workers ✅
- Casual workers ✅
- Part-time workers ✅
- CONTRACT WORKERS ✅ (Don't confuse!)
KEYWORDS: - “Self-employed” = Exempted (no employer) - “Government servants” = Exempted (different scheme) - “Contract workers” = COVERED (employed!)
MEMORY TIP: “SGDF Out, Workers In” (Self/Govt/Domestic/Foreign out; all workers in)

Employer: 1.75% = 🪙🪙🪙 (multiple coins - more than 3x employee)




What is INCLUDED in “Wages”: - ✅ Basic salary - ✅ Allowances (housing, transport, etc.) - ✅ Commissions - ✅ Overtime pay - ✅ Payments for leave (annual leave, sick leave)
What is EXCLUDED from “Wages”:







Excluded Item
Reason




Annual bonus
One-time payment, not regular wages


Employer’s contribution to statutory funds
Employer’s separate obligation (EPF, SOCSO)


Service charge/tips
Not guaranteed, variable


Gratuity
Retirement payment


Retrenchment compensation
Termination payment




📝 EXAM QUESTION 5 (Links to Section 11.5 - Wages Definition)
Question: “Which payments NOT considered wages for SOCSO? I. Annual bonus II. Employer’s contribution to statutory fund III. Payments for leave
A. I and II ✅ B. II and III C. I and III D. None of the above”
Answer: A (I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Regular payments = Wages; One-time/Statutory = NOT wages!
DETAILED ANALYSIS:
I. Annual Bonus ✅ NOT WAGES: - One-time annual payment - Not regular monthly income - Discretionary (not guaranteed) - EXCLUDED from SOCSO contribution calculation
Example:
Employee Monthly Salary: RM3,000
Annual Bonus: RM6,000 (2 months)

SOCSO Contribution Based On:
Monthly: RM3,000 only (NOT RM3,000 + RM500 bonus portion)
II. Employer’s Contribution to Statutory Fund ✅ NOT WAGES: - Employer’s separate legal obligation - Examples: EPF contribution, SOCSO contribution itself - NOT part of employee’s wages - Already separate line item
Example:
Employee Salary: RM3,000
Employer EPF: RM390 (13%)
Employer SOCSO: RM52.50 (1.75%)

Wages for SOCSO calculation: RM3,000 only
(NOT RM3,000 + RM390 + RM52.50)
III. Payments for Leave ❌ IS WAGES (INCLUDED): - Regular income replacement - Annual leave pay, sick leave pay - Part of normal employment terms - INCLUDED in wages calculation
Example:
Employee takes 5 days annual leave
Receives: RM500 leave pay

This RM500 IS included in wages for SOCSO
Contributes: RM500 × 0.5% = RM2.50
WAGES DETERMINATION PRINCIPLE:
INCLUDED (IS Wages):
✅ Regular monthly payments
✅ Guaranteed employment income
✅ Salary, allowances, overtime
✅ Leave payments
✅ Commissions

EXCLUDED (NOT Wages):
❌ One-time bonuses
❌ Employer's statutory contributions
❌ Gratuity/retirement payments
❌ Retrenchment compensation
❌ Tips/service charges (variable)
WHY THIS MATTERS: - Affects contribution calculation - Higher “wages” = Higher contribution - Must know what to include/exclude - Compliance requirement
KEYWORDS: - “Annual bonus” = One-time, NOT wages - “Statutory fund contribution” = Separate, NOT wages - “Leave payments” = Regular, IS wages
MEMORY TIP: “Regular = Wages, One-time = Not Wages”




TWO Types of Employers (CRITICAL):


Definition: - Employer who directly employs the employee - Undertakes payment of wages - Handles all service matters (HR, administration)
Example:
ABC Manufacturing Sdn Bhd
↓ (directly hires)
Factory Worker
↓
ABC pays salary, manages employment
Result: ABC = Principal Employer




Definition: - Contractor/subcontractor who directly supervises work - May not pay wages (principal employer pays) - Employee works under immediate employer’s supervision
Example:
ABC Company (Principal Employer)
↓ (contracts to)
XYZ Contractor (Immediate Employer)
↓ (supervises)
Worker on site
↓
Worker physically works for XYZ
But ABC pays wages

📝 EXAM QUESTION 9 & 10 (Links to Section 11.6 - Employer Types)
Question 9: “Employers under SOCSO categorized into: I. Principal employer II. Immediate employer
A. I only B. II only C. I and II only ✅ D. Neither I nor II”
Answer: C (Both I and II)
Question 10: “Principal Employer refers to: I. Employer who employed employee directly II. Employer who undertakes payment of wages and service matters
A. I only B. II only C. I and II only ✅ D. Neither I nor II”
Answer: C (Both I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: TWO employer types exist; Principal = Direct employment + Wages/Service responsibility!
COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS:
Question 9 - Two Categories: Both categories exist in SOCSO framework: - Principal Employer: Main employer (direct employment, pays wages) - Immediate Employer: On-site supervisor (may be contractor)
Question 10 - Principal Employer Definition: BOTH statements define Principal Employer:
I. Direct Employment ✅: - Hired employee directly - Employment contract with principal - Not through intermediary
II. Payment & Service Matters ✅: - Pays wages to employee - Handles HR administration - Manages employment relationship - Responsible for benefits, leave, etc.
RELATIONSHIP DIAGRAM:
Typical Scenario:

PRINCIPAL EMPLOYER
(Main Company)
    ├── Directly employs ✅
    ├── Pays wages ✅
    ├── Handles service matters ✅
    └── SOCSO registration ✅

IMMEDIATE EMPLOYER
(Contractor/Supervisor)
    ├── Supervises work day-to-day
    ├── May not pay wages
    └── On-site management
PRACTICAL EXAMPLE:
Construction Project:

ABC Developer (Principal Employer):
- Hires construction workers
- Pays monthly salaries
- Manages HR, benefits
- Registers with SOCSO

XYZ Contractor (Immediate Employer):
- Supervises workers on site
- Directs daily work
- Reports to principal
- NOT responsible for SOCSO
RESPONSIBILITY ALLOCATION:



Responsibility

✅ YES
