KEYWORDS: - “Principal employer” = Direct hire + Wage payer - “Immediate employer” = Supervisor/contractor - “Both categories” = Two types exist - “I and II” = Complete definition
MEMORY TIP:
PRINCIPAL = PAYS (wages + contributions)
IMMEDIATE = IN-PERSON (supervision)





📝 EXAM QUESTION 4 (Links to Section 11.7 - SOCSO Key Facts)
Question: “Which TRUE for SOCSO? I. Scheme compulsory except for exempted workers II. If have SOCSO + other insurance, can only claim from one III. After age 60, can still be covered if employer contributes
A. I and II B. II and III C. I and III D. None of the above ✅”
Answer: D (None of the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Statement II and III are FALSE - only Statement I is true, but “None” means all must be true!
STATEMENT ANALYSIS:
I. Scheme compulsory except exempted workers ✅ TRUE: - SOCSO is MANDATORY for eligible workers - Exemptions: Self-employed, government servants, domestic workers, foreign workers - Not optional for covered employees
II. Can only claim from one scheme ❌ FALSE: - Can claim from BOTH SOCSO AND other insurance! - SOCSO is SOCIAL SECURITY, not insurance exclusion - Other insurance (life, PA, medical) INDEPENDENT - Can claim medical from SOCSO + medical insurance - Can receive SOCSO pension + life insurance payout
Example:
Worker injured at work (EIIS coverage):

From SOCSO:
- Medical treatment (free)
- Temporary disablement benefit (RM2,000/month)
- Rehabilitation

From Personal Accident Insurance:
- RM50,000 lump sum payout
- Medical expense reimbursement

Result: CAN CLAIM FROM BOTH! ✅
III. After age 60, can be covered if employer contributes ❌ FALSE: - INVALIDITY scheme: Must be UNDER 60 at diagnosis - EMPLOYMENT INJURY scheme: No age limit for NEW injuries - BUT: Once reach 60, STOP contributing to Invalidity Scheme - NEW employees aged 60+ = Only Employment Injury coverage
Correct Rule:
Employee aged 58:
- Contributes to BOTH schemes ✅

Employee turns 60:
- STOPS contributing to Invalidity Scheme ❌
- CONTINUES Employment Injury coverage only ✅

Employee hired at age 62:
- Only Employment Injury coverage ✅
- NO Invalidity Scheme coverage ❌
WHY “NONE OF THE ABOVE”?: - Statement I: TRUE ✅ - Statement II: FALSE ❌ - Statement III: FALSE ❌ - Question asks which are TRUE - Only I is true, but answer options require multiple true statements - Since II and III are false, answer = None of the above
KEYWORDS: - “Compulsory” = Mandatory (TRUE) - “Only claim from one” = FALSE (can claim multiple) - “After 60 coverage” = FALSE (Invalidity stops at 60)
MEMORY TIP: “SOCSO + Insurance = Both Okay!” (not mutually exclusive)




📝 EXAM QUESTION 1 (Links to Section 11.2 - Mission)
Question: “SOCSO mission statements, which correct? I. Promote work safety/health of workers II. Promote work safety/health of employers III. Strengthen fund through contribution rate review
A. I and II ✅ B. II and III C. I and III D. All the above”
Answer: A (I and II)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Mission focuses on SAFETY promotion (workers AND employers), NOT fund strengthening!
ANALYSIS:
I. Promote work safety/health of WORKERS ✅ MISSION: - Core SOCSO objective - Prevent workplace injuries - Protect employee welfare - Education and awareness programs
II. Promote work safety/health of EMPLOYERS ✅ MISSION: - Encourage safer workplaces - Employer education programs - Incentivize safety compliance - Reduce overall claims
III. Strengthen fund through contribution review ❌ NOT MISSION: - This is OPERATIONAL STRATEGY, not mission - Mission = Social welfare goals - Fund management = Implementation method - Contribution rates = Technical matter
DISTINCTION:
MISSION (What we aim to achieve):
✅ Worker safety and health
✅ Employer safety promotion
✅ Social security protection
✅ Rehabilitation services

STRATEGIES (How we achieve it):
- Fund management
- Contribution rate setting
- Technology adoption
- Service delivery improvement
KEYWORDS: - “Mission” = Core purpose - “Promote safety/health” = Protection objective - “Strengthen fund” = Strategy, not mission




📝 EXAM QUESTION 8 (Links to Section 11.9 - Appeals)
Question: “If employer/employee/dependents not satisfied with SOCSO decision, appeal to: A. SOCSO Board B. Social Security Appellate Board ✅ C. Medical and Hospital Appeal Board D. Social Security Appellate Board” (Note: B and D same - likely typo in original)
Answer: B or D (Social Security Appellate Board)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Appeals go to INDEPENDENT Appellate Board, NOT internal SOCSO Board!
APPEALS STRUCTURE:
STEP 1: SOCSO Decision (claim approval/rejection)
    ↓ (if not satisfied)
STEP 2: Appeal to Social Security Appellate Board
    ↓ (independent review)
STEP 3: Binding Decision
WHY APPELLATE BOARD?: - Independent body (not SOCSO internal) - Ensures fair review - Legal expertise - Quasi-judicial function
KEYWORDS: - “Appeal” = Challenge decision - “Appellate Board” = Independent review body - NOT “SOCSO Board” (internal)

title: Chapter 10: Consumer Protection and Life Insurance Industry Code of Practice
text:
Consumer protection is the cornerstone of modern insurance regulation. This chapter covers the eight basic consumer rights, regulatory frameworks (BNM, FSA 2013), industry associations (LIAM, PIAM), agent professionalism requirements, and the Code of Good Practice.
Exam Weight: 6-8% of total exam
Study Time Recommendation: 5-7 hours




By the end of this chapter, you must be able to:

List and explain the Eight Basic Consumer Rights
Understand regulatory frameworks (FSA 2013, BNM’s role)
Know agent entry requirements and CPD hours
Apply Code of Good Practice provisions
Explain policy surrender and free-look period rules
Identify roles of LIAM, PIAM, and Ombudsman
Understand digital transformation and consumer protection







CRITICAL CONCEPT (HIGH EXAM FREQUENCY) - MEMORIZE ALL EIGHT:
EIGHT BASIC CONSUMER RIGHTS
├── 1. Right to SAFETY
├── 2. Right to INFORMATION
├── 3. Right to CHOICE
├── 4. Right to BE HEARD
├── 5. Right to REDRESS
├── 6. Right to CONSUMER EDUCATION
├── 7. Right to SATISFACTION
└── 8. Right to BASIC GOODS & SERVICES



Definition: Protection against products/services hazardous to health or life.
In Insurance Context: - Products must be financially sound - Insurers must maintain solvency - Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework ensures stability - Protection from mis-selling
Example:
Consumer buys life insurance expecting protection
Insurer must be financially stable to pay claims
BNM monitors insurers' capital adequacy
Ensures claims can be paid when needed




Definition: Access to facts needed to make informed choices.
In Insurance Context: - Product Disclosure Sheet provided before purchase - Clear explanation of benefits, exclusions, charges - Sales illustrations with guaranteed and non-guaranteed benefits - Policy Information Statement after issuance
Key Documents:








Document
When
Content




Product Disclosure Sheet
Before purchase
Features, benefits, exclusions, risks


Sales Illustration
During proposal
Benefit projections, assumptions


Policy Document
After issuance
Full terms and conditions

Premium payment, contact details







Definition: Access to variety of products at competitive prices.
FSA 2013 Enhancements: - Product Comparator Tool - Compare products across insurers - Direct distribution channels - Commission-free pure protection products - Multiple insurers in market (competition) - Online platforms for comparison
Example:
Consumer wants term insurance
Can use Product Comparator to compare:
- Insurer A: RM500/year, sum assured RM500,000
- Insurer B: RM550/year, sum assured RM500,000, critical illness rider
- Insurer C: RM480/year, sum assured RM500,000 (online, no commission)

Makes informed choice based on needs and budget




Definition: Assurance that consumer interests receive consideration.
Mechanisms: - Complaints channels at insurers - Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS) - Independent dispute resolution - BNM supervision of market conduct - Industry associations (LIAM, PIAM) oversight
Complaint Process:
STEP 1: Complaint to Insurer (direct)
↓ (If not satisfied)
STEP 2: Escalate to Insurer's Head Office
↓ (If still not satisfied)
STEP 3: Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS)
↓
Independent review and binding decision




Definition: Fair settlement of just claims, including compensation.
Insurance Context: - Timely claims processing - Fair claims assessment - Compensation for losses - Appeals process available
FSA 2013 Provisions: - Insurers must handle claims professionally - Clear claims procedures - Timely notification of claim decisions - OFS can award compensation up to specified limits




Definition: Acquire knowledge and skills for informed decisions.
BNM Initiatives: - Financial literacy programs - Consumer education websites (e.g., BNMTELELINK, BNMLINK) - Service Guide (from July 1, 2016) - Explains services to expect - Self-assessment tools and financial calculators - Public awareness campaigns
Service Guide Coverage (July 1, 2016): - Before purchasing: Needs analysis, product explanation - When buying: Application assistance, nomination guidance - During term: Policy servicing, claims assistance




Definition: Fulfillment of basic needs for quality of life.
Insurance Context: - Products meet actual needs - Suitable recommendations - Quality service delivery - Professional conduct by agents
Agent’s Role: - Conduct needs analysis (Customer Fact Find) - Recommend suitable products - Provide ongoing service - Act in client’s best interest




Definition: Access to essential goods and services.
Insurance Context: - Basic insurance products accessible to all - Affordable pure protection products - Direct channels (online, walk-in) reduce costs - Commission-free products available (from July 1, 2017)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 4 (Links to Section 10.1 - Eight Basic Rights)
Question: “Which is NOT one of basic rights by International Consumer Movement? A. Right to satisfaction from products/services B. Right to digital access and privacy ✅ C. Right to basic goods and services D. Right to be heard in disputes”
Answer: B (Right to digital access and privacy)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Only EIGHT recognized basic consumer rights - digital access NOT one of them!
THE EIGHT BASIC RIGHTS (memorize): 1. ✅ Safety 2. ✅ Information 3. ✅ Choice 4. ✅ Be Heard 5. ✅ Redress 6. ✅ Consumer Education 7. ✅ Satisfaction (Option A - IS a basic right) 8. ✅ Basic Goods & Services (Option C - IS a basic right)
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ IS a basic right: - Right to Satisfaction (#7) - Products/services meet needs - Quality of life fulfillment
B ❌ NOT a basic right (CORRECT ANSWER): - Digital access/privacy = Modern concern - NOT part of original 8 basic rights - May be covered under other regulations (data protection) - But NOT a recognized consumer right in the traditional list
C ✅ IS a basic right: - Right to Basic Goods & Services (#8) - Access to essential products
D ✅ IS a basic right: - Right to Be Heard (#4) - Consumer interests considered - Complaints mechanisms
KEYWORDS: - “NOT one of” = Identify the exception - “International Consumer Movement” = Eight basic rights - “Digital access and privacy” = Modern issue, not basic right
MEMORY TIP: “Eight Classic Rights” (before digital age) - Digital access came later!

📝 EXAM QUESTION 5 (Links to Section 10.2.1 - Policy Surrender)
Question: “Under FSA 2013, insurer allowed to provide cash value in: I. Single premium policies at any time II. Life policies after 3 years III. Life policies before 3 years
A. i only B. i & ii only C. i & iii only D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: FSA 2013 LIBERALIZED surrender - cash value available in ALL THREE situations!
DETAILED ANALYSIS:
I. Single Premium Policies at ANY TIME ✅ TRUE: - Can surrender immediately or anytime after - No waiting period required - Full cash value provided (subject to charges)
Example:
Buy single premium policy: RM100,000
After 1 year, need money: CAN surrender
Receive: Cash value (e.g., RM95,000 after charges)
II. Life Policies AFTER 3 Years ✅ TRUE: - Regular premium policies in force >3 years - Cash value accumulation - Standard surrender provision
Example:
Buy regular premium policy: RM200/month
Year 4: Want to surrender
Cash value: Available (accumulated over 3+ years)
III. Life Policies BEFORE 3 Years ✅ TRUE: - Even policies <3 years can have cash value - Depends on policy type and premium paid - FSA 2013 allows flexibility
Example:
Buy policy, paid 2 years premiums
Need to surrender after 2 years
May receive cash value (if policy has any accumulated)
More flexible than old Insurance Act 1996
FSA 2013 IMPROVEMENT:
Old Insurance Act 1996:
- Strict 3-year rule
- Limited surrender options
- Less consumer-friendly

FSA 2013:
- More flexible surrender terms
- Consumer empowerment
- Greater control over policies
KEYWORDS: - “Single premium at any time” = Immediate flexibility - “After 3 years” = Standard rule - “Before 3 years” = FSA 2013 liberalization - “All the above” = All three scenarios valid
MEMORY TIP: “FSA 2013 = More Freedom to Surrender” (consumer-friendly reform)




Definition: Period during which policyholder can return policy for refund.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 6 (Links to Section 10.2.2 - Free-Look Period)
Question: “Maggie wants to return policy few days after receiving. According to FSA 2013, which accurately describes her rights? A. Must pay administrative fees + medical costs B. Must return within 15 days for refund minus medical costs ✅ C. Cannot return once issued and delivered D. Must provide detailed written explanation”
Answer: B (Return within 15 days, refund minus medical costs)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: 15-day free-look = Consumer protection, minimal deductions!
CORRECT PROVISION (Option B): - 15 days from policy receipt (not from application) - Full refund of premiums paid - MINUS: Only medical examination costs (if incurred) - NO administrative fees deducted - NO explanation required
Example:
Maggie's Policy Details:
Premium paid: RM5,000
Medical exam cost (paid by insurer): RM300
Administrative costs: RM150

Within 15 Days, She Returns:
Refund: RM5,000 - RM300 = RM4,700
(Medical exam cost deducted only)
NOT deducted: Administrative fees

After 15 Days:
Free-look expired, standard surrender rules apply
WHY OTHERS WRONG:
A ❌ Must pay administrative fees: - FALSE - Only medical costs deducted - Administrative fees NOT charged
C ❌ Cannot return once issued: - FALSE - Can return within 15 days - Free-look period specifically for this
D ❌ Must provide explanation: - FALSE - NO justification needed - Consumer’s absolute right
CONSUMER PROTECTION RATIONALE: - Allows time to review policy - Read and understand terms - Change mind without penalty - Fair to consumer and insurer (medical costs real expense)
KEYWORDS: - “15 days” = Free-look period - “Minus medical costs” = Only deduction - “Full refund” = Consumer protection
MEMORY TIP: “15 Days, Medical Only” (simple refund rule)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 7 (Links to Section 10.3.1 - Agent Requirements)
Question: “Requirements for life insurance agent: I. 18 years of age II. Passed pre-contract examination III. Registration with NAMLIA IV. Registration with LIAM
A. i & ii only B. i, ii & iii C. i, ii & iv ✅ D. All the above”
Answer: C (i, ii & iv)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Register with LIAM (NOT NAMLIA)!
REQUIREMENT ANALYSIS:
I. 18 years of age ✅ CORRECT: - Legal age of majority - Can enter contracts - Minimum requirement by BNM
II. Passed pre-contract examination ✅ CORRECT: - PCEIA - Pre-Contract Examination for Insurance Agents - Administered by MII - OR PCIL - Combined exam (Life + Investment-Linked) - Mandatory before appointment
III. Registration with NAMLIA ❌ WRONG: - NO such organization! - NAMLIA does NOT exist - Common exam trap!
IV. Registration with LIAM ✅ CORRECT: - LIAM - Life Insurance Association of Malaysia - ALL life insurance agents must register - Industry requirement

KEYWORDS: - “18 years” = Minimum age - “Pre-contract examination” = PCEIA/PCIL - “LIAM” = Life Insurance Association Malaysia - “NAMLIA” = Does NOT exist (trap!)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 9 (Links to Section 10.4 - Code Application Date)
Question: “Which TRUE regarding Code of Good Practice for agents/insurers? A. Applies only to products after 1st July 1997 B. Applies to products on or after 1st July 1997 ✅ C. Regulates actual sales talk by agents D. Regulates mortality table selection”
Answer: B (Applies on or after July 1, 1997)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: “ON or AFTER” (inclusive of July 1, 1997) - not “AFTER” (exclusive)!
KEY DISTINCTION:
"AFTER July 1, 1997" = From July 2, 1997 onwards (exclusive)
"ON OR AFTER July 1, 1997" = From July 1, 1997 onwards (inclusive) ✅
ANALYSIS:
A ❌ “Only to products AFTER July 1”: - Would exclude July 1, 1997 itself - WRONG - includes products from July 1 itself
B ✅ “Products ON OR AFTER July 1, 1997”: - CORRECT - inclusive of the date - All products from July 1, 1997 onwards - This is the official application date
C ❌ “Regulates actual sales talk”: - Code focuses on product design, sales illustrations, disclosures - NOT about regulating specific sales conversations - Too narrow interpretation
D ❌ “Regulates mortality table”: - Mortality tables = Actuarial/technical matter - Code focuses on consumer protection, not technical calculations - Wrong scope
WHAT CODE ACTUALLY COVERS: - Product design ethics - Fair pricing - Sales illustrations standards - Disclosure requirements - Proposal form guidelines - Policy information statements
KEYWORDS: - “On or after” = Inclusive date - “July 1, 1997” = Effective date - “Life products” = Scope

📝 EXAM QUESTION 10 (Links to Section 10.4 - Code Objectives)
Question: “Code objectives: I. Design to ethical standards II. Fair pricing III. Truth in selling with disclosures IV. Proper advice to proposers
A. i only B. i & ii only C. i, ii & iii only D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Code has COMPREHENSIVE objectives - all four areas covered!
FOUR KEY OBJECTIVES:
I. Design to Ethical Standards ✅: - Products meet real needs - Not designed to exploit consumers - Suitable product features - Fair terms and conditions
II. Fair Pricing ✅: - Premiums reasonable - Charges transparent - No hidden costs - Value for money
III. Truth in Selling with Full Disclosures ✅: - Accurate sales illustrations - Complete information provided - Material facts disclosed - No misleading representations
IV. Proper Advice to Proposers ✅: - Suitable recommendations - Needs analysis conducted - Client’s best interest - Professional conduct
COMPREHENSIVE PROTECTION:
Product Stage → Objective
────────────────────────────
Design → Ethical standards (I)
Pricing → Fair pricing (II)
Selling → Truth/Disclosure (III)
Advice → Proper guidance (IV)
KEYWORDS: - “All the above” = Comprehensive coverage - “Objectives” = Multiple goals - “Code of Good Practice” = Industry standards

📝 EXAM QUESTION 2 (Links to Section 10.4.1 - Sales Illustrations)
Question: “Which FALSE about sales illustration? A. Actuary reviews assumptions every 2 years B. Information current, accurate, not misleading C. Must contain clear statement of risks D. Should only present guaranteed benefits, avoiding non-guaranteed ✅”
Answer: D (Should only present guaranteed - FALSE)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Sales illustrations MUST show BOTH guaranteed AND non-guaranteed benefits!
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ TRUE statement: - Appointed Actuary reviews assumptions - At least once every 2 years - Ensures appropriateness
B ✅ TRUE statement: - All information must be current - Accurate and not misleading - Consumer protection
C ✅ TRUE statement: - Must clearly state risks - Policy owner understands risks borne - Transparency requirement
D ❌ FALSE statement (CORRECT ANSWER): - Should show BOTH guaranteed AND non-guaranteed - Non-guaranteed benefits with clear assumptions - Complete picture for consumer - NOT limited to guaranteed only
WHY SHOW BOTH?
GUARANTEED Benefits:
- Death benefit (sum assured)
- Guaranteed cash values
- Fixed benefits

NON-GUARANTEED Benefits:
- Investment returns (unit-linked)
- Dividends/bonuses (participating)
- Variable benefits

Consumer needs to see:
- Minimum guaranteed (worst case)
- Potential non-guaranteed (upside)
- Make informed decision
KEYWORDS: - “FALSE” = Identify incorrect statement - “Only guaranteed” = Wrong (too restrictive) - “Both guaranteed and non-guaranteed” = Correct approach
MEMORY TIP: “Show ALL Benefits, Guaranteed + Maybe” (complete picture)




Must Include: - ✅ Premium payment facilities - ✅ Contact person for enquiries/service - ✅ Importance of advising address changes - ❌ NOT legal advice (e.g., will writing) - outside scope

📝 EXAM QUESTION 3 (Links to Section 10.4.2 - Policy Information)
Question: “Policy information statement shall include all EXCEPT: A. Facility for premium payment B. Facility to provide legal advice (will writing) ✅ C. Person to contact for enquiry/service D. Importance of advising address changes”
Answer: B (Legal advice facility - NOT included)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Policy information = POLICY-RELATED info, NOT general legal services!
WHAT’S INCLUDED:
A ✅ Premium payment facilities: - Payment methods available - Payment due dates - Payment channels
C ✅ Contact person: - Who to contact for service - Enquiry channels - Customer service details
D ✅ Address change importance: - Keep insurer updated - Ensure policy documents received - Claims communication
WHAT’S NOT INCLUDED:
B ❌ Legal advice facilities: - Will writing = Separate legal service - NOT part of insurance policy service - Outside scope of policy information - Would need separate legal professional
SCOPE OF POLICY INFORMATION: - Policy-specific services - Insurance-related matters - Ongoing policy administration - NOT general legal/financial advice
KEYWORDS: - “EXCEPT” = Identify what’s NOT included - “Legal advice” = Beyond policy scope - “Policy information” = Policy-related only





Code Requirement: Materials must be accurate and current.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 1 (Links to Section 10.5 - Misleading Materials)
Question: “Zoom Life has misleading brochures due to changed circumstances. What should company do per Code? A. Continue distribution, money already spent B. Continue distribution, no Code violation C. Must withdraw immediately or breach Code ✅ D. Continue with letter to rectify”
Answer: C (Must withdraw immediately or breach Code)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Misleading materials = IMMEDIATE WITHDRAWAL required (consumer protection priority)!
CODE PRINCIPLE: - Accuracy is paramount - Materials must reflect current circumstances - NO misleading information allowed - Consumer protection over company costs
ANALYSIS:
A ❌ Continue because money spent: - Cost is NOT justification for misleading consumers - Consumer protection > Company cost - Violates Code principles
B ❌ Continue, no violation: - FALSE - misleading materials = Code violation - Cannot continue distribution
C ✅ MUST WITHDRAW immediately: - CORRECT - only acceptable action - Prevents consumer harm - Code compliance requirement - Breach if continues
D ❌ Continue with rectification letter: - NOT sufficient - Still distributing misleading materials - Letter doesn’t fix original brochure - Must withdraw, then issue corrected version
PROPER ACTION:
1. STOP distribution immediately ✅
2. Withdraw existing brochures ✅
3. Correct the information ✅
4. Print new accurate materials ✅
5. Then distribute corrected version ✅
KEYWORDS: - “Misleading” = Inaccurate information - “Must withdraw” = Immediate action - “Breach Code” = Violation if continues
MEMORY TIP: “Misleading = STOP NOW” (consumer protection priority)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 8 (Links to Section 10.7 - Code Purpose)
Question: “Which NOT a purpose of Code of Good Practice? A. Encourage digital technologies for customer engagement ✅ B. Regulate sales illustrations for clarity C. Provide guidelines on proposal form disclosures D. Establish guidelines for ethical product design”
Answer: A (Digital technologies - NOT a purpose)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Code focuses on TRADITIONAL consumer protection, not technology adoption!
ACTUAL CODE PURPOSES:
B ✅ IS a purpose: - Regulate sales illustrations - Ensure clarity and transparency - Protect consumers from misleading projections
C ✅ IS a purpose: - Guidelines on proposal form disclosures - Protect consumer interests - Ensure material facts disclosed
D ✅ IS a purpose: - Ethical product design - Products meet actual needs - Fair terms and conditions
NOT A PURPOSE:

CODE FOCUS AREAS: - Product design ethics - Fair pricing - Sales illustration standards - Disclosure requirements - Agent conduct - Consumer protection
KEYWORDS: - “NOT one of purposes” = Identify exception - “Digital technologies” = Modern concern, not original Code purpose - “Code of Good Practice” = Consumer protection focus

Definition: Protection against products/services hazardous to health or life.
In Insurance Context: - Products must be financially sound - Insurers must maintain solvency - Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework ensures stability - Protection from mis-selling
Example:
Consumer buys life insurance expecting protection
Insurer must be financially stable to pay claims
BNM monitors insurers' capital adequacy
Ensures claims can be paid when needed




Definition: Access to facts needed to make informed choices.
In Insurance Context: - Product Disclosure Sheet provided before purchase - Clear explanation of benefits, exclusions, charges - Sales illustrations with guaranteed and non-guaranteed benefits - Policy Information Statement after issuance

Definition: Access to variety of products at competitive prices.
FSA 2013 Enhancements: - Product Comparator Tool - Compare products across insurers - Direct distribution channels - Commission-free pure protection products - Multiple insurers in market (competition) - Online platforms for comparison
Example:
Consumer wants term insurance
Can use Product Comparator to compare:
- Insurer A: RM500/year, sum assured RM500,000
- Insurer B: RM550/year, sum assured RM500,000, critical illness rider
- Insurer C: RM480/year, sum assured RM500,000 (online, no commission)

Makes informed choice based on needs and budget




Definition: Assurance that consumer interests receive consideration.
Mechanisms: - Complaints channels at insurers - Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS) - Independent dispute resolution - BNM supervision of market conduct - Industry associations (LIAM, PIAM) oversight
Complaint Process:
STEP 1: Complaint to Insurer (direct)
↓ (If not satisfied)
STEP 2: Escalate to Insurer's Head Office
↓ (If still not satisfied)

↓
Independent review and binding decision




Definition: Fair settlement of just claims, including compensation.
Insurance Context: - Timely claims processing - Fair claims assessment - Compensation for losses - Appeals process available
FSA 2013 Provisions: - Insurers must handle claims professionally - Clear claims procedures - Timely notification of claim decisions - OFS can award compensation up to specified limits




Definition: Acquire knowledge and skills for informed decisions.
BNM Initiatives: - Financial literacy programs - Consumer education websites (e.g., BNMTELELINK, BNMLINK) - Service Guide (from July 1, 2016) - Explains services to expect - Self-assessment tools and financial calculators - Public awareness campaigns
Service Guide Coverage (July 1, 2016): - Before purchasing: Needs analysis, product explanation - When buying: Application assistance, nomination guidance - During term: Policy servicing, claims assistance




Definition: Fulfillment of basic needs for quality of life.
Insurance Context: - Products meet actual needs - Suitable recommendations - Quality service delivery - Professional conduct by agents
Agent’s Role: - Conduct needs analysis (Customer Fact Find) - Recommend suitable products - Provide ongoing service - Act in client’s best interest




Definition: Access to essential goods and services.
Insurance Context: - Basic insurance products accessible to all - Affordable pure protection products - Direct channels (online, walk-in) reduce costs - Commission-free products available (from July 1, 2017)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 4 (Links to Section 10.1 - Eight Basic Rights)
Question: “Which is NOT one of basic rights by International Consumer Movement? A. Right to satisfaction from products/services B. Right to digital access and privacy ✅ C. Right to basic goods and services D. Right to be heard in disputes”
Answer: B (Right to digital access and privacy)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Only EIGHT recognized basic consumer rights - digital access NOT one of them!
THE EIGHT BASIC RIGHTS (memorize): 1. ✅ Safety 2. ✅ Information 3. ✅ Choice 4. ✅ Be Heard 5. ✅ Redress 6. ✅ Consumer Education 7. ✅ Satisfaction (Option A - IS a basic right) 8. ✅ Basic Goods & Services (Option C - IS a basic right)
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ IS a basic right: - Right to Satisfaction (#7) - Products/services meet needs - Quality of life fulfillment
B ❌ NOT a basic right (CORRECT ANSWER): - Digital access/privacy = Modern concern - NOT part of original 8 basic rights - May be covered under other regulations (data protection) - But NOT a recognized consumer right in the traditional list
C ✅ IS a basic right: - Right to Basic Goods & Services (#8) - Access to essential products
D ✅ IS a basic right: - Right to Be Heard (#4) - Consumer interests considered - Complaints mechanisms
KEYWORDS: - “NOT one of” = Identify the exception - “International Consumer Movement” = Eight basic rights - “Digital access and privacy” = Modern issue, not basic right
MEMORY TIP: “Eight Classic Rights” (before digital age) - Digital access came later!

📝 EXAM QUESTION 5 (Links to Section 10.2.1 - Policy Surrender)
Question: “Under FSA 2013, insurer allowed to provide cash value in: I. Single premium policies at any time II. Life policies after 3 years III. Life policies before 3 years
A. i only B. i & ii only C. i & iii only D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: FSA 2013 LIBERALIZED surrender - cash value available in ALL THREE situations!
DETAILED ANALYSIS:
I. Single Premium Policies at ANY TIME ✅ TRUE: - Can surrender immediately or anytime after - No waiting period required - Full cash value provided (subject to charges)
Example:
Buy single premium policy: RM100,000
After 1 year, need money: CAN surrender
Receive: Cash value (e.g., RM95,000 after charges)
II. Life Policies AFTER 3 Years ✅ TRUE: - Regular premium policies in force >3 years - Cash value accumulation - Standard surrender provision
Example:
Buy regular premium policy: RM200/month
Year 4: Want to surrender
Cash value: Available (accumulated over 3+ years)
III. Life Policies BEFORE 3 Years ✅ TRUE: - Even policies <3 years can have cash value - Depends on policy type and premium paid - FSA 2013 allows flexibility
Example:
Buy policy, paid 2 years premiums
Need to surrender after 2 years
May receive cash value (if policy has any accumulated)
More flexible than old Insurance Act 1996
FSA 2013 IMPROVEMENT:
Old Insurance Act 1996:
- Strict 3-year rule
- Limited surrender options
- Less consumer-friendly

FSA 2013:
- More flexible surrender terms
- Consumer empowerment
- Greater control over policies
KEYWORDS: - “Single premium at any time” = Immediate flexibility - “After 3 years” = Standard rule - “Before 3 years” = FSA 2013 liberalization - “All the above” = All three scenarios valid
MEMORY TIP: “FSA 2013 = More Freedom to Surrender” (consumer-friendly reform)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 6 (Links to Section 10.2.2 - Free-Look Period)
Question: “Maggie wants to return policy few days after receiving. According to FSA 2013, which accurately describes her rights? A. Must pay administrative fees + medical costs B. Must return within 15 days for refund minus medical costs ✅ C. Cannot return once issued and delivered D. Must provide detailed written explanation”
Answer: B (Return within 15 days, refund minus medical costs)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: 15-day free-look = Consumer protection, minimal deductions!
CORRECT PROVISION (Option B): - 15 days from policy receipt (not from application) - Full refund of premiums paid - MINUS: Only medical examination costs (if incurred) - NO administrative fees deducted - NO explanation required
Example:
Maggie's Policy Details:
Premium paid: RM5,000
Medical exam cost (paid by insurer): RM300
Administrative costs: RM150

Within 15 Days, She Returns:
Refund: RM5,000 - RM300 = RM4,700
(Medical exam cost deducted only)
NOT deducted: Administrative fees

After 15 Days:
Free-look expired, standard surrender rules apply
WHY OTHERS WRONG:
A ❌ Must pay administrative fees: - FALSE - Only medical costs deducted - Administrative fees NOT charged
C ❌ Cannot return once issued: - FALSE - Can return within 15 days - Free-look period specifically for this
D ❌ Must provide explanation: - FALSE - NO justification needed - Consumer’s absolute right
CONSUMER PROTECTION RATIONALE: - Allows time to review policy - Read and understand terms - Change mind without penalty - Fair to consumer and insurer (medical costs real expense)
KEYWORDS: - “15 days” = Free-look period - “Minus medical costs” = Only deduction - “Full refund” = Consumer protection
MEMORY TIP: “15 Days, Medical Only” (simple refund rule)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 9 (Links to Section 10.4 - Code Application Date)
Question: “Which TRUE regarding Code of Good Practice for agents/insurers? A. Applies only to products after 1st July 1997 B. Applies to products on or after 1st July 1997 ✅ C. Regulates actual sales talk by agents D. Regulates mortality table selection”
Answer: B (Applies on or after July 1, 1997)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: “ON or AFTER” (inclusive of July 1, 1997) - not “AFTER” (exclusive)!
KEY DISTINCTION:
"AFTER July 1, 1997" = From July 2, 1997 onwards (exclusive)
"ON OR AFTER July 1, 1997" = From July 1, 1997 onwards (inclusive) ✅
ANALYSIS:
A ❌ “Only to products AFTER July 1”: - Would exclude July 1, 1997 itself - WRONG - includes products from July 1 itself
B ✅ “Products ON OR AFTER July 1, 1997”: - CORRECT - inclusive of the date - All products from July 1, 1997 onwards - This is the official application date
C ❌ “Regulates actual sales talk”: - Code focuses on product design, sales illustrations, disclosures - NOT about regulating specific sales conversations - Too narrow interpretation
D ❌ “Regulates mortality table”: - Mortality tables = Actuarial/technical matter - Code focuses on consumer protection, not technical calculations - Wrong scope
WHAT CODE ACTUALLY COVERS: - Product design ethics - Fair pricing - Sales illustrations standards - Disclosure requirements - Proposal form guidelines - Policy information statements
KEYWORDS: - “On or after” = Inclusive date - “July 1, 1997” = Effective date - “Life products” = Scope

📝 EXAM QUESTION 10 (Links to Section 10.4 - Code Objectives)
Question: “Code objectives: I. Design to ethical standards II. Fair pricing III. Truth in selling with disclosures IV. Proper advice to proposers
A. i only B. i & ii only C. i, ii & iii only D. All the above ✅”
Answer: D (All the above)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Code has COMPREHENSIVE objectives - all four areas covered!
FOUR KEY OBJECTIVES:
I. Design to Ethical Standards ✅: - Products meet real needs - Not designed to exploit consumers - Suitable product features - Fair terms and conditions
II. Fair Pricing ✅: - Premiums reasonable - Charges transparent - No hidden costs - Value for money
III. Truth in Selling with Full Disclosures ✅: - Accurate sales illustrations - Complete information provided - Material facts disclosed - No misleading representations
IV. Proper Advice to Proposers ✅: - Suitable recommendations - Needs analysis conducted - Client’s best interest - Professional conduct
COMPREHENSIVE PROTECTION:
Product Stage → Objective
────────────────────────────
Design → Ethical standards (I)
Pricing → Fair pricing (II)
Selling → Truth/Disclosure (III)

📝 EXAM QUESTION 2 (Links to Section 10.4.1 - Sales Illustrations)
Question: “Which FALSE about sales illustration? A. Actuary reviews assumptions every 2 years B. Information current, accurate, not misleading C. Must contain clear statement of risks D. Should only present guaranteed benefits, avoiding non-guaranteed ✅”
Answer: D (Should only present guaranteed - FALSE)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Sales illustrations MUST show BOTH guaranteed AND non-guaranteed benefits!
ANALYSIS:
A ✅ TRUE statement: - Appointed Actuary reviews assumptions - At least once every 2 years - Ensures appropriateness
B ✅ TRUE statement: - All information must be current - Accurate and not misleading - Consumer protection
C ✅ TRUE statement: - Must clearly state risks - Policy owner understands risks borne - Transparency requirement
D ❌ FALSE statement (CORRECT ANSWER): - Should show BOTH guaranteed AND non-guaranteed - Non-guaranteed benefits with clear assumptions - Complete picture for consumer - NOT limited to guaranteed only
WHY SHOW BOTH?
GUARANTEED Benefits:
- Death benefit (sum assured)
- Guaranteed cash values
- Fixed benefits

NON-GUARANTEED Benefits:
- Investment returns (unit-linked)
- Dividends/bonuses (participating)
- Variable benefits

Consumer needs to see:
- Minimum guaranteed (worst case)
- Potential non-guaranteed (upside)
- Make informed decision
KEYWORDS: - “FALSE” = Identify incorrect statement - “Only guaranteed” = Wrong (too restrictive) - “Both guaranteed and non-guaranteed” = Correct approach
MEMORY TIP: “Show ALL Benefits, Guaranteed + Maybe” (complete picture)




Must Include: - ✅ Premium payment facilities - ✅ Contact person for enquiries/service - ✅ Importance of advising address changes - ❌ NOT legal advice (e.g., will writing) - outside scope

📝 EXAM QUESTION 3 (Links to Section 10.4.2 - Policy Information)
Question: “Policy information statement shall include all EXCEPT: A. Facility for premium payment B. Facility to provide legal advice (will writing) ✅ C. Person to contact for enquiry/service D. Importance of advising address changes”
Answer: B (Legal advice facility - NOT included)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Policy information = POLICY-RELATED info, NOT general legal services!
WHAT’S INCLUDED:
A ✅ Premium payment facilities: - Payment methods available - Payment due dates - Payment channels
C ✅ Contact person: - Who to contact for service - Enquiry channels - Customer service details
D ✅ Address change importance: - Keep insurer updated - Ensure policy documents received - Claims communication
WHAT’S NOT INCLUDED:
B ❌ Legal advice facilities: - Will writing = Separate legal service - NOT part of insurance policy service - Outside scope of policy information - Would need separate legal professional
SCOPE OF POLICY INFORMATION: - Policy-specific services - Insurance-related matters - Ongoing policy administration - NOT general legal/financial advice
KEYWORDS: - “EXCEPT” = Identify what’s NOT included - “Legal advice” = Beyond policy scope - “Policy information” = Policy-related only





Code Requirement: Materials must be accurate and current.

📝 EXAM QUESTION 1 (Links to Section 10.5 - Misleading Materials)
Question: “Zoom Life has misleading brochures due to changed circumstances. What should company do per Code? A. Continue distribution, money already spent B. Continue distribution, no Code violation C. Must withdraw immediately or breach Code ✅ D. Continue with letter to rectify”
Answer: C (Must withdraw immediately or breach Code)
🔑 KEY INSIGHT: Misleading materials = IMMEDIATE WITHDRAWAL required (consumer protection priority)!
CODE PRINCIPLE: - Accuracy is paramount - Materials must reflect current circumstances - NO misleading information allowed - Consumer protection over company costs
ANALYSIS:
A ❌ Continue because money spent: - Cost is NOT justification for misleading consumers - Consumer protection > Company cost - Violates Code principles
B ❌ Continue, no violation: - FALSE - misleading materials = Code violation - Cannot continue distribution
C ✅ MUST WITHDRAW immediately: - CORRECT - only acceptable action - Prevents consumer harm - Code compliance requirement - Breach if continues
D ❌ Continue with rectification letter: - NOT sufficient - Still distributing misleading materials - Letter doesn’t fix original brochure - Must withdraw, then issue corrected version
PROPER ACTION:
1. STOP distribution immediately ✅
2. Withdraw existing brochures ✅
3. Correct the information ✅
4. Print new accurate materials ✅
5. Then distribute corrected version ✅
KEYWORDS: - “Misleading” = Inaccurate information - “Must withdraw” = Immediate action - “Breach Code” = Violation if continues
MEMORY TIP: “Misleading = STOP NOW” (consumer protection priority)

Question: “Which NOT a purpose of Code of Good Practice? A. Encourage digital technologies for customer engagement ✅ B. Regulate sales illustrations for clarity C. Provide guidelines on proposal form disclosures D. Establish guidelines for ethical product design”

NOT A PURPOSE:

title: Chapter 8: Takaful (Islamic Insurance)
text:
Exam Weight: 8-10% | Study Time: 5-6 hours





Why Conventional Insurance is Haram (Forbidden): 1. Al-Gharar (Uncertainty/Ambiguity) - Q1 2. Al-Maisir (Gambling/Speculation) - Q2
3. Al-Riba (Interest/Usury) - Q3
Memory: GMR = Gharar, Maisir, Riba





Al-Quran (Word of Allah) - Highest authority
Al-Sunnah (Prophet’s practices)
Ijma (Scholarly consensus)
Qiyas (Analogical reasoning)





Origin: Kafala = To guarantee, safeguard, preserve
Answer: C (Kafala)




1. AL-MUDHARABAH (Profit-Sharing Model) - Q8, Q9 - Operator Role: Mudarib (Entrepreneur) - Participant Role: Capital providers
- Profits: SHARED per agreed ratio (e.g., 70:30) - Losses: PARTICIPANTS bear (unless operator negligent)
2. WAKALAH (Agency Model) - Q10 - Operator Role: Wakeel (Agent) - Earnings: Fixed Wakalah fee (not profit share) - Profits: ALL to participants - Losses: Participants bear
Memory: MW Models = Mudharabah + Wakalah

Definition: Part of contribution given as donation to help fellow participants
How it works:
Contribution Split:
- Tabarru portion → Mutual pool (for claims)
- Savings portion → Personal account
Purpose: Eliminates gharar/maisir through mutual assistance




Three Conditions for Valid Transaction (ALL required): 1. Deliverable - Subject can be delivered 2. Identified - Type and quantity specified 3. Date determined - Delivery timeline clear
Memory: DID = Deliverable, Identified, Date
Answer: D (All the above)




Family Takaful: - Similar to life insurance (Shariah-compliant) - Long-term savings + protection - Whole life, endowment, investment-linked

title: Chapter 1: Understanding Risks
text:
This chapter forms the foundation of risk management and insurance planning. It explores fundamental concepts that will be tested extensively in the exam. Mastering the distinctions between risk, peril, and hazard is critical for exam success.
Exam Weight: This is a foundational chapter - expect 10-15% of exam questions from this material.
Study Time Recommendation: 8-10 hours




By the end of this chapter, you must be able to:

Define and distinguish between risk, peril, and hazard with precision
Classify different types of risks (fundamental, particular, pure, speculative, etc.)
Identify how human behaviour influences risk perception and assessment
Apply demographic factors to predict risk tolerance
Evaluate client risk tolerance using both qualitative and quantitative methods









Risk = “Uncertainty about financial loss from an exposure”
⚠️ EXAM ALERT: This is THE definition you must know word-for-word. Do NOT confuse with general definitions of risk from other contexts.
Two Forms of Loss: 1. Actual Losses - Losses that have already occurred 2. Potential Losses (Loss Exposures) - Possible future losses













Term
Definition
Example
Memory Aid




Peril
The SOURCE or CAUSE of loss
Fire, theft, death, illness
“P” for “Problem that causes”


Hazard
CONDITION that INCREASES probability/severity of loss
Slippery road, smoking, carelessness
“H” for “Helper of loss”



⚠️ COMMON EXAM TRAP: Students often reverse peril and hazard. Remember: Peril CAUSES, Hazard INCREASES













Hazard Type
Definition
Malaysian Example
Exam Tip




Physical Hazard
Tangible condition increasing loss likelihood
Overweight individual with family history of hypertension; oil-spilled road
Look for PHYSICAL characteristics in scenarios


Moral Hazard
Dishonesty/character flaws increasing loss
Fabricating insurance claims; pre-existing conditions not disclosed
Watch for FRAUD and DISHONESTY keywords


Morale Hazard
Indifference/carelessness due to insurance
Not locking doors because “I have insurance”; speeding because “car is insured”
Remember: “Morale = More Careless”



📌 MEMORY TRICK: - Moral = Immoral (dishonest) - Morale = Low morale (don’t care attitude)




Case Study: Mr. Lim (Overweight with Hypertension History)
Facts: - 40 years old - Overweight - Family history of hypertension
Insurance Implications: 1. Higher premiums due to elevated risk 2. More stringent underwriting process 3. Potential for policy exclusions or loading
Malaysian Context Example: - Prevalence of diabetes and heart disease in Malaysia - Higher incidence among certain ethnic groups - Impact of Malaysian diet (high sugar, high carb)
⚠️ EXAM SCENARIO ALERT: Questions may present similar cases and ask you to: - Identify the type of hazard (PHYSICAL) - Recommend appropriate insurance solutions - Suggest risk mitigation strategies




Key Characteristics: 1. Risk-taking behaviour knowing insurer pays 2. Fraudulent claims 3. Erosion of trust
Malaysian Example: Early Medical Card Claim - Policyholder submits expensive medical claim shortly after purchase - Investigation reveals pre-existing condition - Constitutes moral hazard through non-disclosure
⚠️ EXAM TIP: If scenario mentions “shortly after policy purchase” + “expensive claim” = likely testing moral hazard concept




Case Study: Mr. Alex (Comprehensive Insurance, Careless Behaviour)
Characteristics: - Has comprehensive coverage - Leaves car unlocked - Doesn’t secure home - Takes unnecessary risks
Why This is Morale Hazard (NOT Moral): - No fraud or dishonesty - Simply careless because “insurance will cover” - Attitude: “Why bother being careful?”
📌 EXAM DISTINCTION: - Moral = Intentional dishonesty - Morale = Unintentional carelessness












Aspect
Risk
Chance




Focus
Possibility of LOSS
Possibility of GAIN


Outcome
Unfavourable/Negative
Favourable/Positive


Example
Business failure
Winning lottery


In Malaysian Context
Café failing in competitive F&B sector
Winning Sports Toto



⚠️ EXAM ALERT: Questions may present scenarios asking you to identify whether something represents “risk” or “chance” - focus on whether outcome is gain or loss.




The Critical Triangle (MEMORIZE THIS RELATIONSHIP):
HAZARD → Increases likelihood → PERIL → Causes → RISK (Possibility of Loss)
Example Chain: 1. Hazard: Smoking (physical hazard) 2. Peril: Heart disease 3. Risk: Financial loss from medical expenses/death
Table: Risk-Peril-Hazard in Insurance Contexts









Concept
Life Insurance
Medical Insurance
Malaysian Example




Risk
Financial loss from death of breadwinner
Financial burden from medical expenses
Loss of income affecting children’s education; high hospital costs


Peril
Death from illness, accident, natural causes
Medical condition requiring treatment
Death from common Malaysian health issues (heart disease, diabetes); road accidents


Hazard
Smoking, dangerous hobbies, lifestyle
High-risk occupation, extreme sports
Construction work in Malaysia; popular extreme sports (jungle trekking)



⚠️ EXAM STRATEGY: When given a scenario, systematically identify: 1. What is the RISK (financial loss potential)? 2. What is the PERIL (what causes the loss)? 3. What are the HAZARDS (what increases the likelihood)?







6 Major Risk Categories (Know distinctions cold):










Risk Type
Definition
Characteristics
Insurability
Examples




Fundamental Risks
Affect entire economy/large groups
Widespread impact; impersonal; often societal/natural
Usually NOT insurable
Hyperinflation, earthquakes, war, climate change, pandemic


Particular Risks
Affect only individuals
Personal; limited impact
Generally INSURABLE
Robbery, house fire, car theft


Dynamic Risks
Result from changes in economy/society
Unpredictable; evolving
Difficult to insure
Technological change, regulatory changes, digital economy risks


Static Risks
Result from irregular events
Stable; predictable patterns
Easily insurable
Death, fire (normal occurrence)


Pure Risks
Only loss or no loss (no gain)
No opportunity for profit
INSURABLE
Property damage, liability, premature death


Speculative Risks
Possibility of loss OR gain
Investment nature
NOT insurable
Stock market, business ventures, gambling







Climate Change Impact on Malaysia:
Real-World Examples: 1. Severe flooding in Eastern states (Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang) 2. Changing monsoon patterns affecting agriculture 3. Rising sea levels threatening coastal areas
Economic Consequences: - Infrastructure damage - Agricultural disruption (rubber, palm oil plantations) - Tourism sector impact - Insurance underwriting challenges
Technological Advancement: Digital Economy
Malaysian Context: - Rapid e-commerce growth - Digital finance adoption (e-wallets, fintech) - New risks: Cybersecurity, digital fraud, data breaches
⚠️ EXAM TIP: If question mentions “affects entire community/economy” or “cannot prevent individually” → Fundamental Risk




Case Study: Mr. Lee’s Home Security
Scenario: - Urban homeowner in Kuala Lumpur - Concerned about burglaries - Individual risk (not community-wide)
Mitigation Actions: 1. Install CCTV systems 2. Hire security guards 3. Join neighbourhood watch 4. Install alarm systems
Key Point: Individual can reduce this risk through personal action
⚠️ EXAM DISTINCTION: - Fundamental Risk = Cannot control individually - Particular Risk = Can control through personal action




Characteristics: - Result from changes in society/economy - Difficult to predict - Continuously evolving
Malaysian Examples: 1. Technology: Shift to Industry 4.0, automation replacing jobs 2. Regulatory: Changes in EPF/SOCSO regulations 3. Economic: Currency fluctuations, trade policy changes 4. Digital Transformation: E-invoice implementation, digital tax systems




Characteristics: - Regular occurrence patterns - Predictable through statistics - Stable over time
Examples: - Death (mortality tables) - Fire occurrence (historical data) - Accident frequency (actuarial data)
📌 Memory Aid: “Static” = “Statistics” = Predictable from data




Key Characteristic: Only two possible outcomes - Loss or No Loss (NEVER a gain)
Properties: 1. Insurable 2. Fortuitous (happens by chance) 3. Definite and measurable 4. Large number of similar exposures
Examples: - Premature death - Property damage - Disability - Liability claims
⚠️ EXAM ALERT: Pure risk questions often test understanding that there is NO possibility of gain




Key Characteristic: Three possible outcomes - Loss, No Change, OR Gain
Properties: 1. NOT insurable 2. Voluntarily undertaken 3. Potential for profit
Examples: - Stock market investments - Business ventures - Currency trading - Property speculation
📌 EXAM TIP: If scenario involves potential profit/gain → Speculative Risk → NOT INSURABLE
















Type
Definition
Based On
Example




Objective Risk
Actual, measurable risk based on facts/statistics
Data, evidence, actuarial tables
Statistical probability of car accident based on traffic data


Perceived Risk
Individual’s subjective assessment of risk
Personal beliefs, emotions, experience
Feeling air travel is dangerous despite safety statistics



Malaysian Example: - Perceived: Many Malaysians fear flying (post-MH370) - Objective: Air travel statistically safer than driving on Malaysian highways
⚠️ EXAM SCENARIO: “Alan feels scuba diving is dangerous even though it’s safe with proper training” - This is PERCEIVED RISK (not objective risk)




Three Main Categories:









Category
Attitude
Behaviour
Investment Profile




Risk Averse
Views risk as danger
Avoids uncertainty; prefers safety
Fixed deposits, bonds, conservative investments


Risk Neutral
Indifferent to risk
Focuses on expected return regardless of risk
Balanced approach


Risk Seeking
Views risk as opportunity
Actively pursues risk for higher returns
Aggressive equity investments, speculative assets



Special Category:
Thrill Seeker = Person who consistently seeks out or creates risks in ALL life situations - NOT just in investments - In all aspects of life (sports, career, lifestyle)
⚠️ EXAM TRAP: Don’t confuse “risk seeking” (investment style) with “thrill seeker” (lifestyle)




Cognitive Biases (Common Exam Topics):









Bias
Definition
Malaysian Example
Impact




Availability Bias
Recent/memorable events disproportionately influence decisions
Reading about insurance claim rejection in newspaper, then fearing all insurers won’t pay
Overestimate likelihood of rare events


Overconfidence Bias
Excessive confidence in own judgment
Investor thinks they can time the market
Underestimate risks


Anchoring Bias
Over-rely on first piece of information
First premium quote becomes reference point
Poor comparison


Confirmation Bias
Seek information confirming existing beliefs
Only read success stories about property investment
Ignore warning signs



Malaysian Exam Scenario - Availability Bias: “Ah Fatt reads newspaper article about insurer not paying claim. Now concerned about buying life insurance.” - This is AVAILABILITY BIAS (recent information overly influences decision)
⚠️ EXAM STRATEGY: When scenario shows someone making irrational decision based on one incident → likely testing availability bias




Critical Distinction for Exam:








Aspect
Risk Taker
Thrill Seeker




Scope
Specific contexts (e.g., investments)
ALL life situations


Motivation
Higher returns/rewards
Excitement itself


Rationality
Can be rational (calculated risk)
Often irrational


Example
Entrepreneur starting business
Base jumper, extreme sports enthusiast







Key Demographic Factors (HIGH EXAM PROBABILITY):








Factor
Impact on Risk Tolerance
Explanation




Age
Younger → Higher tolerance
More time to recover from losses



Older → Lower tolerance
Need capital preservation


Wealth
Wealthier → Higher tolerance
Can afford losses



Less wealthy → Lower tolerance
Cannot afford losses


Occupation
Stable job → Can take more investment risk
Secure income stream



Unstable job → Lower investment risk tolerance
Need liquidity


Family Size
More dependents → Lower tolerance
Greater financial responsibilities



Fewer dependents → Higher tolerance
Less obligations


Education
Higher education → Often higher tolerance
Better understanding of risk/return


Cultural Factors
Varies by culture
Malaysian context: Different ethnic groups may have different savings/investment cultures



⚠️ EXAM QUESTION PATTERN: “Choose correct combination of demographic characteristics that influence risk tolerance” - ANSWER: Wealth, Age, Occupation (Family size often included)

















Approach
Method
Advantages
Disadvantages
When to Use




Qualitative
Interviews, discussions, open-ended questions
Rich insights, understand motivations
Subjective, hard to compare
Initial assessment, understanding context


Quantitative
Standardized questionnaires, numerical scoring
Objective, comparable, consistent
May miss nuances
Formal risk profiling, documentation



Best Practice: Use BOTH approaches for comprehensive assessment




Poor Question Examples: ❌ “Are you a risk taker?” (Too vague) ❌ “Do you like risk?” (Unclear context)
Good Question Examples: ✅ “If your investment portfolio decreased by 20% in one year, would you: a) Sell immediately, b) Hold, c) Buy more?” ✅ “What is the maximum percentage loss you could tolerate in one year before you would want to change your investment strategy?”
Malaysian Context Questions: ✅ “Would you invest in Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) or equity unit trusts?” ✅ “How comfortable are you investing outside EPF contributions?”




Five Critical Areas:

Risk Capacity (Financial ability to take risk)

Net worth
Income stability
Emergency funds
Debt levels

Risk Tolerance (Psychological comfort with risk)

Emotional reactions
Sleep-at-night factor
Past experiences

Risk Required (Risk needed to meet goals)

Financial goals
Time horizon
Return requirements

Risk Perception (How client views risk)

Subjective assessment
Influenced by biases
Cultural factors

Risk Behaviour (How client actually acts)

Past investment decisions
Portfolio composition
Response to market volatility


⚠️ EXAM ALERT: Don’t confuse risk CAPACITY (ability) with risk TOLERANCE (willingness)




Analysis Framework:








Portfolio Characteristic
What It Indicates
Malaysian Example




High equity allocation
Higher risk tolerance OR misunderstanding of risk
80% in Bursa Malaysia stocks


Multiple insurance policies
Risk averse OR sophisticated risk management
Life, medical, critical illness, investment-linked all with different insurers


Frequent job changes
Risk taking OR career growth focus
Moving between MNCs every 2-3 years


Variable income
Risk taking (entrepreneur) OR industry norm
Full-time business owner vs commission-based sales


Property investments
Risk seeking OR cultural preference
Multiple properties (Malaysian preference for property)











Profile: - Age: 35 - Just sold successful startup - Diversified investment portfolio - No dependents
Question: Primary strategy for next financial steps?
Options Analysis: - A. Reinvest all in new startup → ❌ Too risky, no diversification - B. Balanced portfolio, long-term growth → ✅ CORRECT - C. Significant portion to fixed deposits → ❌ Too conservative for age/profile - D. High-risk, high-return → ❌ Assumes entrepreneurial = risk seeking in all areas
Answer: B
Rationale: - Age 35 = Long time horizon - Successful exit = Has capital - No dependents = Can take some risk - Already entrepreneurial = Don’t need 100% high risk - Balanced approach best aligns with situation
⚠️ EXAM TIP: Don’t assume entrepreneur wants all high-risk. Consider complete profile.




Profile: - Age: 50 - Teacher (stable income) - Risk-averse - Most savings in fixed deposits and bonds - Planning for retirement
Question: How to advise for retirement preparation?
Options Analysis: - A. Maintain current strategy → ❌ Too conservative, won’t grow enough - B. Gradually shift to higher-yielding options → ✅ CORRECT - C. Immediately diversify into high-risk stocks → ❌ Against risk profile - D. Invest in overseas markets → ❌ Doesn’t match risk tolerance
Answer: B
Rationale: - Age 50 = Still 10-15 years to retirement - Risk-averse = Must respect tolerance - “Gradually” = Not shocking to client - “Higher-yielding” ≠ “high-risk” - Can improve returns without drastically increasing risk
⚠️ EXAM TIP: “Gradually” is key word showing respect for client’s risk aversion




Profile: - Age: 40 - IT professional in Penang - Moderate risk appetite - Stable job - Unfamiliar with stock investments
Question: Approach to assess suitability for stock market investment?
Options Analysis: - A. Structured questionnaire to evaluate knowledge and risk tolerance → ✅ CORRECT - B. Immediately recommend blue-chips → ❌ Skips assessment - C. High-risk portfolio (stable job justification) → ❌ Ignores lack of knowledge - D. Advise against due to lack of familiarity → ❌ Too restrictive
Answer: A
Rationale: - “Unfamiliar” = Need education assessment - Moderate risk appetite = Need to verify - Structured approach = Professional standard - Must assess BEFORE recommending
⚠️ EXAM TIP: When client lacks knowledge, ALWAYS assess first before recommending




Profile: - Age: 28 - Freelance graphic designer - Goal: Buy house in 5 years - Some savings - Moderately aggressive risk tolerance
Question: Which investment strategy aligns best?
Options Analysis: - A. High-risk for higher returns → ❌ Too risky for 5-year goal - B. Conservative (government bonds) → ❌ Too conservative for profile - C. Balanced mix of equities and bonds → ✅ CORRECT - D. Solely real estate → ❌ Need liquidity for house down payment
Answer: C
Rationale: - 5 years = Medium-term - Moderately aggressive = Can handle some volatility - Specific goal = Need balance between growth and stability - Equities = Growth potential - Bonds = Stability component
⚠️ EXAM TIP: Match investment strategy to BOTH risk tolerance AND time horizon








Risk: “Uncertainty about financial loss from an exposure”
Peril: The source or cause of loss
Hazard: Condition that increases probability/severity of loss
Pure Risk: Only loss or no loss (never gain) - INSURABLE
Speculative Risk: Loss, no change, OR gain - NOT INSURABLE
Fundamental Risk: Affects entire economy/large groups - Usually NOT INSURABLE
Particular Risk: Affects only individuals - Generally INSURABLE














Trap
What Students Think
Reality
How to Avoid




Moral vs Morale
Same thing
Different: Moral = dishonest, Morale = careless
Remember: Moral = Immoral (fraud)


Risk vs Chance
Interchangeable
Risk = focus on loss, Chance = focus on gain
Look for gain/loss in scenario


Peril vs Hazard
Same thing
Peril causes, Hazard increases
Peril = Problem, Hazard = Helper


Entrepreneur = Risk Seeker
All entrepreneurs are risk seeking
May be calculated, not seeking risk for thrill
Analyze complete profile


Insurance = Solution
Insurance solves all risks
Only solves PURE risks
Check if speculative or fundamental risk















If Question Contains…
Likely Testing…
Key Words to Watch




“Shortly after policy purchase” + “expensive claim”
Moral hazard
Pre-existing, undisclosed, fraud


“Don’t bother locking car because insured”
Morale hazard
Careless, indifferent, complacent


“Affects entire economy/community”
Fundamental risk
Widespread, cannot control, economy-wide


“Can prevent through personal action”
Particular risk
Individual, personal, controllable


“Potential for profit”
Speculative risk
Gain, investment, business


“Only loss or no loss”
Pure risk
No gain, insurable


“Recent news article influences decision”
Availability bias
Recent, memorable, newspaper


“Combination of demographics”
Age, wealth, occupation
NOT population density, NOT evidence








Common Health Issues: Heart disease, diabetes (mention in physical hazard scenarios)
Popular Investments: ASB, property, EPF (mention in risk tolerance examples)
Insurance Products: Life, medical, investment-linked (mention in scenarios)
Cultural Factors: Property preference, multi-generational planning
Regulatory Bodies: BNM, LIAM, PIAM (know their roles)
Local Events: Flooding (fundamental risk), burglary in urban areas (particular risk)








1. In financial planning, risk is best defined as: - A. The chance of an investment loss - B. Uncertainty about financial loss from an exposure ✅ - C. The chance of a physical loss - D. The chance of an income loss
Exam Tip: This is a word-for-word definition question. Other options are incomplete.

2. Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between peril and hazard? - A. Peril increases the likelihood of loss; hazard causes the loss - B. Peril causes the loss; hazard increases the likelihood of loss ✅ - C. They are interchangeable terms - D. Peril is insurable; hazard is not
Exam Tip: Most common mix-up in the exam. Remember: Peril CAUSES, Hazard INCREASES.

3. Mr. Ahmad leaves his car unlocked in a shopping mall parking lot because he has comprehensive insurance. This is an example of: - A. Physical hazard - B. Moral hazard - C. Morale hazard ✅ - D. Speculative risk
Exam Tip: No fraud (not moral), just carelessness due to insurance (morale).

4. A policyholder submits a claim for a pre-existing medical condition that was not disclosed during application. This represents: - A. Physical hazard - B. Moral hazard ✅ - C. Morale hazard - D. Fundamental risk
Exam Tip: Non-disclosure/fraud = Moral hazard

5. Fire that burns down a house is an example of: - A. Risk - B. Peril ✅ - C. Hazard - D. Loss exposure
Exam Tip: Fire is the CAUSE of loss = Peril

6. Storing flammable materials near an electrical panel is an example of: - A. Peril - B. Pure risk - C. Physical hazard ✅ - D. Moral hazard
Exam Tip: Tangible condition that increases likelihood = Physical hazard

7. The possibility of financial loss due to the death of a breadwinner represents: - A. Peril - B. Risk ✅ - C. Hazard - D. Pure loss
Exam Tip: “Possibility of loss” = definition of Risk

8. Which statement about risk and chance is correct? - A. Both focus on unfavorable outcomes - B. Risk focuses on loss; chance focuses on gain ✅ - C. They are synonymous in financial planning - D. Chance is always insurable; risk is not
Exam Tip: Key distinction is loss vs. gain focus

9. Being overweight with a family history of diabetes is classified as what type of hazard for life insurance? - A. Moral hazard - B. Morale hazard - C. Physical hazard ✅ - D. Speculative hazard
Exam Tip: Physical/health condition = Physical hazard

10. In the risk-peril-hazard relationship, what role does hazard play? - A. Causes the loss to occur - B. Represents the possibility of loss - C. Increases the likelihood or severity of loss ✅ - D. Provides insurance coverage
Exam Tip: Hazard is the “multiplier” of risk




11. Severe flooding affecting multiple states in Malaysia is an example of: - A. Particular risk - B. Fundamental risk ✅ - C. Pure risk only - D. Dynamic risk only
Exam Tip: Affects large groups/economy = Fundamental. (Can also be pure, but “fundamental” is the best answer for the widespread impact)

12. A house fire affecting only one family is: - A. Fundamental risk - B. Particular risk ✅ - C. Speculative risk - D. Dynamic risk
Exam Tip: Affects only individual/family = Particular

13. Which of the following is a speculative risk? - A. Death of a key employee - B. Fire destroying inventory - C. Starting a new business venture ✅ - D. Liability claim from customer injury
Exam Tip: Only speculative risk has potential for GAIN

14. Premature death is classified as: - A. Pure risk ✅ - B. Speculative risk - C. Dynamic risk - D. Fundamental risk
Exam Tip: Only loss or no loss (no gain possibility) = Pure risk

15. The rapid growth of e-commerce in Malaysia creating cybersecurity risks is an example of: - A. Static risk - B. Dynamic risk ✅ - C. Pure risk - D. Particular risk
Exam Tip: Results from changes in economy/technology = Dynamic

16. Which type of risk is generally NOT insurable? - A. Pure risk - B. Particular risk - C. Static risk - D. Speculative risk ✅
Exam Tip: Speculative risks (potential for gain) are NOT insurable

17. Death following predictable mortality patterns represents: - A. Dynamic risk - B. Static risk ✅ - C. Fundamental risk - D. Speculative risk
Exam Tip: Predictable from statistics = Static risk

18. Which combination correctly matches risk types with insurability? - A. Pure risk - insurable; Speculative risk - not insurable ✅ - B. Fundamental risk - always insurable; Particular risk - not insurable - C. Dynamic risk - insurable; Static risk - not insurable - D. All risks are insurable if premium is high enough
Exam Tip: Pure vs Speculative is the key insurability distinction




19. Alan feels scuba diving is dangerous even though statistics show it’s safe with proper training. Alan’s judgment is based on: - A. Objective risk - B. Risk indifference - C. Risk aversion - D. Perceived risk ✅
Exam Tip: Personal belief vs. facts = Perceived risk

20. A person who is “consistently seeking out or creating risks in ALL life situations” is termed a: - A. Risk seeker - B. Thrill seeker ✅ - C. Risk neutral person - D. Speculative investor
Exam Tip: “ALL life situations” is key phrase = Thrill seeker

21. Ah Fatt reads a newspaper article about an insurer not paying a claim and becomes concerned about buying life insurance. This is an example of: - A. Rationality bias - B. Availability bias ✅ - C. Intimacy bias - D. Confirmation bias
Exam Tip: Recent memorable information disproportionately influences decision = Availability bias

22. A person who prefers government employment for job security would most likely be: - A. Risk averse ✅ - B. Risk indifferent - C. Thrill seeking - D. Risk seeking
Exam Tip: Prefers security/certainty = Risk averse

23. Which factor does NOT affect an individual’s ability to think rationally about risk? - A. Perception of the risk - B. When one does not face a detriment from the risk ✅ - C. Overconfidence - D. Individual’s beliefs and value system
Exam Tip: If no detriment (no stake in outcome), rationality is less affected

24. Objective risk is best defined as: - A. Risk involving loss of face - B. Risk based on person’s beliefs and value system - C. Risk involving loss of freedom - D. Risk based on facts and statistical evidence ✅
Exam Tip: “Objective” = based on facts/data, not emotions




25. Which combination of demographic characteristics most influences attitude toward risk? - A. Wealth, age, and family size - B. Family size, marital status, and sex - C. Family size, age, and population density - D. Wealth, age, and occupation ✅
Exam Tip: This exact question is in the book. Wealth, age, occupation are the key three.

26. A person willing to accept high returns for an increase in risk level is: - A. Risk tolerant ✅ - B. Risk averse - C. Risk indifferent - D. Irrational
Exam Tip: Higher return for higher risk acceptance = Risk tolerant

27. When assessing a client’s risk tolerance, a financial planner should: - A. Find out the client’s net worth only - B. Understand the client’s risk tolerance level ✅ - C. Always recommend lower risk investments - D. Advise additional insurance only
Exam Tip: Understanding risk tolerance is fundamental to financial planning

28. A 28-year-old with no dependents would generally have: - A. Lower risk tolerance than a 50-year-old with three children - B. Higher risk tolerance than a 50-year-old with three children ✅ - C. Same risk tolerance regardless of dependents - D. No ability to assess risk tolerance
Exam Tip: Younger age + no dependents = Higher risk capacity and often higher tolerance

29. Which is the BEST method for assessing a client’s risk tolerance? - A. Qualitative approach only - B. Quantitative approach only - C. Combination of both qualitative and quantitative approaches ✅ - D. Assessing current portfolio only
Exam Tip: Best practice uses BOTH methods for comprehensive assessment

30. A client’s current portfolio consisting of 90% equities and 10% bonds most likely indicates: - A. Risk aversion - B. Conservative risk tolerance - C. Higher risk tolerance ✅ - D. Lack of investment knowledge
Exam Tip: High equity allocation typically indicates higher risk tolerance (or lack of knowledge - but “most likely” = higher tolerance)








B - Exact definition from textbook
B - Peril causes, hazard increases
C - Carelessness due to insurance = morale hazard
B - Non-disclosure/fraud = moral hazard
B - Fire is the cause/source = peril
C - Tangible condition = physical hazard
B - Possibility of loss = risk
B - Key distinction between risk and chance
C - Health/physical condition = physical hazard
C - Hazard increases likelihood/severity





B - Affects large groups = fundamental
B - Affects individual = particular
C - Business has potential for gain = speculative
A - Only loss or no loss = pure
B - Results from economic/tech change = dynamic
D - Speculative risks not insurable
B - Predictable patterns = static
A - Pure insurable, speculative not





D - Belief vs facts = perceived risk
B - ALL life situations = thrill seeker
B - Recent news influences = availability bias
A - Prefers security = risk averse
B - No stake = rationality less affected
D - Objective = based on facts





D - Wealth, age, occupation (from textbook)
A - Accept higher risk for return = tolerant
B - Understanding tolerance is key
B - Younger + no dependents = higher tolerance
C - Both methods best
C - High equity = higher tolerance

Understand and practice distinguishing moral vs morale hazard
Master the 6 types of risks and their characteristics
